    "171fb2185a25edcf71d8281f0eb4d3c2626eccc7": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-09T13:56:58Z",
      "body": "Work package 4 of the plan to move the interactive session verb to Pi. An\nopencode-go/<model> id names the endpoint; it now starts the pinned Pi in the\nTerminal window, with discovery off and one policy extension loaded from a copy\nin the session's private directory, the declared model, and the prompt after\n`--`. The runner checks the pin with require_pi, confirms by `pi --help` in a\nscratch home that the extension's flag is listed, and refuses otherwise,\nremoving what it made. It hands over no key and sets no agent directory: Pi\nsigns in from the maintainer's own ~/.pi/agent (Q-6). A prompt that starts with\n@ is refused, because Pi would read it as a file name.\n\nThe seven OpenCode-only functions, AGENT and GUARDED are gone. The tests get a\npi stand-in beside codex and osascript, and an opencode stand-in that must\nnever be called; the 25 canned effective-policy answers are replaced by tests of\nthe version pin, the read-back, the @ prompt, the scratch home and the absence\nof a key. 19 planted faults in the runner all turn a test red.\n\nDocuments that describe the verb to a reader still say OpenCode until package 5.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01JBF4iPyVeFMJtPjpuSYhYZ\n",

    "36b4b356ca029bc73d971a6bef30a7331c1c944d": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-14T18:59:01Z",
      "body": "The tree baseline is measured only for a run with protected work - the one\ncase that reuses cheap results across the admission. A seconds-only job\n(docs, drift) and a cheap pass that ended blocking red rely on no baseline,\nso they no longer refuse over an unmeasurable or moving tree (L2-3, L2-8).\nEvery ending - green, red, refused, refused admission - goes through one\nfinish(): the refused run names the gates it did not run, prints a banner\nand closes its history record red (L2-2). The cheap phase's not-run header\nnames every blocking red gate instead of claiming a stop at the first\n(L2-7). A refusal names the paths that moved. The worker rule lives once in\nverify_run.worker_bound, used by the full and the targeted check (L2-6).\nThe gates' default interpreter comes from the env argument (L2-9).\n\nL2-1 is rejected: ruff and pytest self-ignore their caches; the new proof\ntest_real_tool_caches_keep_the_baseline_stable runs both inside a checkout\nwithout user-level excludes and stays stable.\n\nOrchestrator hand edit (Opus subagent, maintainer's word of 2026-11-14).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",

    "82a013b92bfab78830cdeeb982d597e217216c64": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-20T11:20:58Z",
      "body": "Main brings the shared two-phase scheduler (scripts/verify_run.py, PR #416,\nbead coding-harness-bxxt.6), venv_guard (PR #415) and the journal citation\ngate (PR #418). The slip counter (bead coding-harness-bxxt.7) is carried into\nmain's structure; nothing of either side is reverted.\n\nConflict resolutions:\n\n- scripts/verify_duration.py: main's in-process writers stay (record_start,\n  record_gate, record_end with root, state_root and env). The slip counter's\n  comparison evidence is attached to them: record_start records\n  common_git_dir for its root, reads the runner-owned comparison variables\n  from the scheduler's env (_comparison_fields(env), falling back to the\n  process environment for the CLI), and creates the targeted history beside\n  the duration history under the same state root at the first version-2\n  marker. append_event/_open_history take both the slip counter's\n  `destination` (the targeted history) and main's keyword `state_root`;\n  targeted_history_path accepts a state root too. Imports keep both\n  Sequence and dataclass/field; _git and _gate_file_digest take main's form.\n  New COMPARISON_ENV_NAMES lists the three variables.\n- scripts/stage2.py: main's scheduler path stays the one full check. The\n  slip counter's single entry point full_verify(root, env, key, change,\n  prepare) is kept, now built on main's body: prepare runs first, outside\n  any admission (main's intent for the full-mode attempt), then\n  intent-to-add, then _scheduled_verify with\n  verify_duration.full_run_context(_checked_tree(root, change), change)\n  added to the scheduler's environment. verify_attempt's full mode hands its\n  preparation (format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, prepare_derived) to\n  full_verify as `prepare` instead of duplicating the intent-to-add,\n  scheduler and cleanup block (house rule 9: one path).\n- scripts/verify_run.py (no conflict, one addition): after recording the\n  start, run_verification drops the comparison variables from the gates'\n  environment, so a gate never inherits them and a check a gate starts is\n  never recorded as a second full run of the same change and tree.\n- tests/test_stage2.py: both sides' new tests kept. The slip end-to-end test\n  now uses the world's committed gate list instead of creating its own\n  decisions/ folder, and its `make` stub is the scheduler's protected gate:\n  it records nothing (the scheduler records start, gate and end) and fails if\n  it inherits the comparison context.\n- tests/test_verify_duration.py: the slip counter's version of the\n  derived-never-persisted test (the reader `slips` is exposed) replaces\n  main's deferral assertions; main's criterion-8 completion-context test is\n  kept.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9DrQg7dkn7zUzrqUEk\n",

      "body": "A rule whose name starts with `secret:` is not applied to a file under the\nrepository's top-level tests/ folder: the working file, and the hunks of a\ncommit patch or of the staged diff that name such a file. Every other rule\nscans tests/ as before, and a secret rule scans everything outside it\n(tests_extra/, docs/tests/, a change's own folder, a link under tests/, a\ncommit message, a prompt text). A diff header that cannot be read with\ncertainty (a quoted name) is scanned in full.\n\nMaintainer's decision of 2026-10-07 on open item O-4 of the stage-2 change;\nthe accepted consequence is that a real key committed in a test file is not\nfound. The secret patterns live in the maintainer's denylist, not in this\nscript, so the marker is a name prefix and each machine sets it itself.\n\nThe log now runs with --no-renames (the staged scan already did) so a diff\nheader names one path, and splits message from patch by a marker line the log\nformat writes. Docstring and WORKFLOW state the exemption.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",

    "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0": {
      "author_utc": "2026-09-30T14:07:20Z",
      "body": "A feature can decide something that belongs in an architecture decision\nrecord, and nothing here asked. Each change anchor now states its class;\na feature states its name and a proposal, and owes an answer file\ndecisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml in the LakeSwitch pilot's format, so\nLakeSwitch can read it unchanged.\n\nscripts/check_adr_answers.py is the gate and the one reader of the\nformat: strict YAML (a duplicate key is refused, a bare no is a boolean),\nevery rule of the answer file, active and archived anchors, one report\nline per cause, exit 0/1/3. It holds existence and format only; it cannot\nsee who wrote or merged an answer, and no line claims it.\n\nscripts/harness.py decide adr asks each open question in a terminal, or\nrecords one answer the maintainer stated elsewhere (--change, --answer,\n--reason, --stated-in). It writes the answer files and a commit message\nwhere git says, and never stages, commits, pushes or merges. Who answered\ncomes from provenance.yaml, which now maps decisions/answers/ to\nhuman-decided with owner_role framework-architect.\n\nThe gate is in decisions/gates.yaml (block, not floor), ci.yml is\nregenerated, both scripts and their tests travel with the kit and the\nanswers do not. The kit probe's exemption for\ntest_the_two_manifests_really_disagree_somewhere is struck and its cap\nlowered to 31: with four more mechanism files the throwaway repository\npasses that test now.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "92c486212d234bfc0af49abcff9bc8bbfa4888d0",
      "subject": "feat(adr): the gate adr-answers and the command decide adr",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "provenance.yaml"
      ]
    },

    "bfc7cad6c84f758b0bee914199912eff602ca6f2": {
      "author_utc": "2026-11-15T11:10:00Z",
      "body": "A second finding on the guard's binding tracking (after F6-4 and F6-5)\nends case repair. The guard now enumerates every way Python binds a\nname - plain and multiple-target assignment, tuple and list unpacking\npaired element-wise, starred, annotated and augmented assignment, the\nwalrus (bound in the enclosing function), for and comprehension targets,\nwith-as, parameter defaults, imports, definitions, except-as, match\ncaptures and del - and repeats until no new log binding appears. Every\nsuch binding shadows an enclosing one; comprehensions are scopes.\n\nA pathlib read_text, read_bytes, write_text or write_bytes is judged by\nits receiver only; its first argument counts only when called on a path\nclass or as a bare function. write_text's content is no destination.\n\nRed-first samples BINDING_FORMS, BINDING_SHADOWS and\nRECEIVER_DESTINATION; the spec's Boundary names what static analysis\ncannot follow (attributes, calls, unpairable containers, order).\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "bfc7cad6c84f758b0bee914199912eff602ca6f2",
      "subject": "fix(flaky-swarm-leak-test): the guard follows every binding form (F6-6, F6-7)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [

      ]
    },

    "db13ce677d6be80fbf4c27da876e8b7b31e7f4be": {
      "author_utc": "2026-10-30T13:44:32Z",
      "body": "Each admission publishes a random token with its ownership and hands it\nto its children through HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_TOKEN. A marker is honoured\nonly when the published ownership names its pid and its token and the\nlock is held. The token reaches every descendant across new sessions,\nnested runners and a dead holder, and no unrelated process knows it; the\nancestry and session proofs are removed.\nspec.md gains a Boundary section, decided by the maintainer on\n2026-10-30: the admission protects load, not data; a descendant outliving\nthe admission after a hard-killed intermediate is an accepted limit.\nThe re-check row F6-5 is rejected as that accepted limit.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9E3xwLQJNC9qs5SWhu\n",
      "body_truncated": false,
      "hash": "db13ce677d6be80fbf4c27da876e8b7b31e7f4be",
      "subject": "fix(verify-machine-lock): an admission token proves nested work; the spec names the boundary (bead coding-harness-p6mu)",
      "touched_mapped_paths": [
        "scripts/stage2.py",
        "tests/test_stage2.py",
        "tests/test_verify_lock.py"
      ]
    },

      "author_utc": "2026-10-30T18:04:23Z",
      "body": "Phase-6 row F6-9: a signal between Popen and the assignment that hands\nthe child to the cleanup left the protected group running. The\nspec Boundary names this and, on the maintainer's word (2026-10-30,\n+30 min, structural), makes any further signal-timing finding an\naccepted limit. Red-first: the new test fails without the deferral.\n\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01UGYZ9E3xwLQJNC9qs5SWhu\n",

          "excerpt": "def _scan(\n    text: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    rules: list[Rule],\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    kind: str = \"file\",\n    *,\n    exempt: bool = False,\n    patch: bool = False,\n    first: int = 1,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Report each match as a place, a rule name and a length. Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "_scan",

          "supported": true,

          "excerpt": "def test_a_commit_patch_that_touches_tests_follows_the_same_split(folder: str, repo: Path, split: Path) -> None:\n    commit_and_remove(repo, f\"{folder}/test_fixture.py\", f'KEY = \"{SECRET}\"\\n')\n    result = run_check(repo, split)\n    assert result.verdict.exit_code() == CLEAN, rendered(result)\n    assert result.commits == 4\n\n    sha = commit_and_remove(repo, f\"{folder}/test_name.py\", f'NAME = \"{CUSTOMER}\"\\n')\n    blocked = run_check(repo, split)\n    assert blocked.verdict.exit_code() == BLOCKED\n    assert f\"commit {sha}:\" in rendered(blocked) and \"rule 'customer'\" in rendered(blocked)\n    assert \"secret:planted\" not in rendered(blocked)\n",

      "statement": "The existing per-hunk exemption is a header-driven state machine: `_scan` sets `in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)` whenever a line starts with one of `DIFF_HEADERS`, and that one boolean then governs every following line of that file's part until the next header. The granularity is the whole file part; `scripts/` contains no parsing of `@@` hunk headers, so added, context and removed lines are not distinguished anywhere today."

          "end_line": 202,
          "excerpt": "def _header_in_tests(line: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a diff header names a file under `tests/` - and only when that is certain.\n\n    With rename detection off, a `diff --git` header reads `a/<path> b/<path>`: the path is the one the\n    equal halves leave, which holds for a name with spaces too. A quoted name, or a header that does not\n    split in two equal halves, is not certain, and \"not certain\" is \"not under tests/\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if line.startswith((\"diff --cc \", \"diff --combined \")):\n        path = line.split(\" \", 2)[2]\n    else:\n        rest = line[len(\"diff --git \") :]\n        size = (len(rest) - 5) // 2\n        path = rest[2 : 2 + size]\n        if rest != f\"a/{path} b/{path}\":\n            return False\n    return path.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX)\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "_header_in_tests",
          "start_line": 187,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "tests/test_leakcheck.py::test_a_name_that_is_hard_to_read_in_a_header_is_exempt_or_scanned_never_mixed_up",
          "end_line": 615,
          "excerpt": "def test_a_name_that_is_hard_to_read_in_a_header_is_exempt_or_scanned_never_mixed_up(\n    name: str, repo: Path, split: Path\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A space and a non-ASCII letter are read with certainty; a quoted name is not, and then the check blocks.\"\"\"\n    commit_and_remove(repo, f\"tests/{name}\", f'KEY = \"{SECRET}\"\\n')\n    result = run_check(repo, split)\n    if '\"' in name:\n        assert result.verdict.exit_code() == BLOCKED, \"a header that cannot be read with certainty is scanned in full\"\n    else:\n        assert result.verdict.exit_code() == CLEAN, rendered(result)\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "tests/test_leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "test_a_name_that_is_hard_to_read_in_a_header_is_exempt_or_scanned_never_mixed_up",
          "start_line": 606,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "`_header_in_tests` decides from the header string alone: for `diff --cc`/`diff --combined` it takes the path after the third field, for `diff --git` it requires the two halves to be equal (`a/<p> b/<p>`) and returns False otherwise.           "excerpt": "def _scan(\n    text: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    rules: list[Rule],\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    kind: str = \"file\",\n    *,\n    exempt: bool = False,\n    patch: bool = False,\n    first: int = 1,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Report each match as a place, a rule name and a length. Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_audit_only(before: bytes, after: bytes) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admit runner call lines under any heading, comparing all remaining input bytes.\n\n    Remove each call's blank separator with it and permit append's current-date\n    header stamp. All other bytes, including reviewer sessions and verdicts,\n    remain review inputs and must match HEAD.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    call = re.compile(\n        rb\"\\n\\nStage-2 call, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}: [a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?: \\(loop marks\\))?\"\n        rb\"(?: \\xc2\\xb7 attempt [1-9]\\d* \\xc2\\xb7 route [a-z0-9-]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 endpoint [a-z0-9-]+ \\xc2\\xb7 model [A-Za-z0-9_./:+-]+(?: \\xc2\\xb7 reason [^\\r\\n]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 leak check clean over \\d+ files, \\d+ commits, \\d+ rules\\.(?=\\n|$)\"\n    )\n    clean_before, clean_after = call.sub(b\"\", before), call.sub(b\"\", after)\n    if clean_before == clean_after:\n        return True\n    try:\n        stamped = check_frontmatter_current.stamped(clean_before.decode(\"utf-8\"), clock_now().local_date).encode(\n            \"utf-8\"\n        )\n    except UnicodeDecodeError:\n        return False\n    return stamped == clean_after\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::bounded_review_diff",
          "end_line": 3030,
          "excerpt": "def bounded_review_diff(diff: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"The prompt's diff, cut at `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES`, and what the cut left out.\n\n    The caller writes the second half into the round record: a clean answer over a cut diff is not a\n    clean answer about the change, and the record must say which of the two it was. The free round is\n    bounded too (R-12 of the review-swarm review): it carries the same diff, and an uncapped prompt\n    would read as a limit that is none.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Split on \"\\n\" only, as git counts: `splitlines()` also splits on CR and form feed, which inflates the\n    # count and rewrites the kept part's line ends (O191-4).\n    lines = diff.split(\"\\n\")\n    if lines and lines[-1] == \"\":\n        lines.pop()\n    if len(lines) <= REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES:\n        return diff, None\n    note = f\"the change diff was cut at {REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES} of {len(lines)} lines\"\n    return \"\\n\".join([*lines[:REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES], f\"## ({note}; the rest is not carried)\"]), note\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "bounded_review_diff",
          "start_line": 3014,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "The two prompt shapes that carry a diff differ in what follows it: `free_round_prompt` puts the diff last, after `FREE_REVIEW_BODY`, the head and `ANSWER_FORMAT`, while `_review_round.prompt_for` appends `READ_REQUEST` once more after `## The diff`, and `bounded_review_diff` appends a markdown note line (`## (the change diff was cut at ...)`) after the last carried hunk. Read with the existing header-driven switch, any line after the final hunk belongs to that last file's part."

Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",

          "excerpt": "def _scan(\n    text: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    rules: list[Rule],\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    kind: str = \"file\",\n    *,\n    exempt: bool = False,\n    patch: bool = False,\n    first: int = 1,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Report each match as a place, a rule name and a length. Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",

          "end_line": 340,
          "excerpt": "def _checked_probe(\n    runner,\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    endpoint: str,\n    model: str,\n    audit: list[str],\n    admission=None,\n    verb: str = \"prepare-explore\",\n    text: str = PROBE_TEXT,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The declaration, the exact-prompt leak check and the audit line - for this one probe, immediately before it.\n\n    `admission` (root, model -> problem or None) replaces the research declaration check for the review\n    swarm's free class (ADR 0021, decision 3); the leak check stays mandatory either way.\n    \"\"\"\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), root, [(\"prompt\", text)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise runner.Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the probe does not start.\")\n    # Re-read admission after the scan, which can cross the terms' UTC cutoff.\n    # Do not record a call or dispatch a probe on yesterday's admission.\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    audit.append(\n        f\"{verb} · endpoint {endpoint} · model {model} · leak check clean over \"\n        f\"{result.files} files, {result.commits} commits, {result.rules} rules.\"\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_audit_only(before: bytes, after: bytes) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admit runner call lines under any heading, comparing all remaining input bytes.\n\n    Remove each call's blank separator with it and permit append's current-date\n    header stamp. All other bytes, including reviewer sessions and verdicts,\n    remain review inputs and must match HEAD.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    call = re.compile(\n        rb\"\\n\\nStage-2 call, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}: [a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?: \\(loop marks\\))?\"\n        rb\"(?: \\xc2\\xb7 attempt [1-9]\\d* \\xc2\\xb7 route [a-z0-9-]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 endpoint [a-z0-9-]+ \\xc2\\xb7 model [A-Za-z0-9_./:+-]+(?: \\xc2\\xb7 reason [^\\r\\n]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 leak check clean over \\d+ files, \\d+ commits, \\d+ rules\\.(?=\\n|$)\"\n    )\n    clean_before, clean_after = call.sub(b\"\", before), call.sub(b\"\", after)\n    if clean_before == clean_after:\n        return True\n    try:\n        stamped = check_frontmatter_current.stamped(clean_before.decode(\"utf-8\"), clock_now().local_date).encode(\n            \"utf-8\"\n        )\n    except UnicodeDecodeError:\n        return False\n    return stamped == clean_after\n",

          "citation": "scripts/run_report.py::call_rows",
          "end_line": 318,
          "excerpt": "def call_rows(findings_text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The findings' Stage-2 call lines as bounded rows of explicitly recorded metadata.\n\n    These are evidence of a call, never measured attempts: no verdict is\n    inferred (a clean leak check is not a completion), absent fields say\n    `not read`, and rows are never joined on their attempt number.\n    \"\"\"\n    if stage2_runs is None:\n        return [\"  calls: not read (runner call reader unavailable)\"]\n    rows = []\n    for line in findings_text.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(stage2_runs.CALL_PREFIXES):\n            continue\n        matched = stage2_runs.CALL_LINE.match(line)\n        kind = matched.group(1) if matched else \"\"\n        rest = matched.group(\"rest\") if matched else \"\"\n        cells = rest.split(\" · \")\n        verb = \"session\" if kind == \"session\" else cells[0].strip() if len(cells) > 1 else \"\"\n        if not verb or len(verb) > FIELD_CAP:\n            verb = \"unparsed\"\n        fields = dict.fromkeys(CALL_FIELDS, NOT_READ)\n        verdict = \"verdict not recorded\"\n        for cell in cells if kind == \"session\" else cells[1:]:\n            key, _, value = cell.partition(\" \")\n            if key in CALL_FIELDS and 0 < len(value) <= FIELD_CAP:\n                fields[key] = value.strip()\n            if kind == \"session\":\n                dispatch = re.fullmatch(r\"dispatch (accepted|pending|failed)(?: \\(.*\\))?\\.\", cell)\n                if dispatch:\n                    verdict = f\"dispatch {dispatch.group(1)}\"\n        rows.append(\n            f\"  call: {verb} · attempt {fields['attempt']} · route {fields['route']}\"\n            f\" · endpoint {fields['endpoint']} · model {fields['model']} · {verdict}\"\n        )\n    return rows\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/run_report.py",
          "reference": "call_rows",
          "start_line": 284,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "The call-line format is pinned byte-level by three independent consumers: the phase-6 admission regex in `review_audit_only` requires the line to end `\\d+ rules\\.` and admits nothing after it; the run measure in `stage2_runs.py` counts a call as clean by the substring `CLEAN = 'leak check clean over'` and parses lines with `CALL_LINE`; and `run_report.call_rows` splits the ` · ` cells. Any tail added to the line (an exemption count) must update `review_audit_only` at the same time or phase 6 refuses every run's audit; `run_report.call_rows` drops unknown cells silently."

          "end_line": 1936,
          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 89,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead ",

      "statement": "`checked_prompt` is the single pre-call choke point (house rule 9, 'one entry point and one writer per action') and it hands `leakcheck.check` a plain string labelled `\"prompt\"`; there is no mechanism today by which a prompt text is marked as a diff, and `_read_prompt_files` likewise reads whole texts.           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `fi",

          "excerpt": "def _header_in_tests(line: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a diff header names a file under `tests/` - and only when that is certain.\n\n    With rename detection off, a `diff --git` header reads `a/<path> b/<path>`: the path is the one the\n    equal halves leave, which holds for a name with spaces too. A quoted name, or a header that does not\n    split in two equal halves, is not certain, and \"not certain\" is \"not under tests/\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if line.startswith((\"diff --cc \", \"diff --combined \")):\n        path = line.split(\" \", 2)[2]\n    else:\n        rest = line[len(\"diff --git \") :]\n        size = (len(rest) - 5) // 2\n        path = rest[2 : 2 + size]\n        if rest != f\"a/{path} b/{path}\":\n            return False\n    return path.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX)\n",

What cannot be scanned is not checked.\",\n            )\n        # else: listed and gone from the disk - nothing to read there; a staged deletion shows in the index scan.\n\n    scanned: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for path in (*change_files, *tree_files):\n        scanned.setdefault(path.relative_to(root).as_p",

          "citation": "AGENTS.md::House rules",
          "end_line": 89,
          "excerpt": "## House rules\n\n1. **The repository is English** — documents, code, identifiers, comments, messages, tests, commit messages and PR\n   bodies. German is the language of the conversation with the maintainer and of the texts the maintainer's display\n   shows at run time (`tools/claude-code/`), nothing else. German that is still in the tree (2026-09-29: mainly\n   `scripts/`, `tests/` and `docs/governance/`) is translated in pull requests of its own, never in passing inside an\n   unrelated change (bead coding-harness-yim).\n2. **Beads only.** The tracker is the Dolt database under `.beads/`, transported via `refs/dolt/data` on origin. No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8). Auto-export is off, and no\n   rendered copy is committed (bead coding-harness-1jg.3): a local reader renders fresh through\n   `scripts/bead_render.py`. Because the diff no longer shows tracker changes, a pull request names in its body every\n   bead it opens, changes or closes (maintainer, 2026-09-23).\n5. **The handover is the file, not the chat.** Session end → a file under `docs/journal/handover/`. A number without\n   its commit or date reads as a historical one — every count carries its cut-off.\n6. **The customer instance is out of bounds.** What is needed from the customer instance (private, never named)\n   travels as a *requirement*, never as an expression — no filename, field name, entity or layer name from there\n   appears in a framework artifact.\n7. **Texts carry their own meaning.** A reader without this session must understand every sentence; bead ids and file\n   names go in parentheses as a suffix, never as the carrier of a sentence.\n8. **A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request** (ADR 0008). A pull request touching a file\n   `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` is a decision PR: title `decide(<scope>): …`, label `decision`, body\n   from the decision template (`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md`). Record an ADR answer only as the\n   maintainer stated it (`python3 scripts/harness.py decide adr … --stated-in …`), never one of your own. Merge only\n   when the maintainer asks in the conversation, after restating the decision block (`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The\n   merge\"); `.claude/settings.json` asks before every merge command it recognises — a brake, not a lock: another\n   spelling passes (`docs/WORKFLOW.md`).\n9. **O",

          "excerpt": "## Q-2 · Which diff lines are exempt\n\nasked: 2026-11-01\nanswer: only added (+) lines in tests/ are exempt; context and removed lines stay checked.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which lines of a tests/ hunk the exemption covers.\n  Intention: keep the exemption as narrow as the bead needs.\n  Today: no exemption in prompts.\n  Repository change: Options: added lines only; added and context lines; the whole hunk.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of the exempt hunks, facing added lines only or wider, we decided on added lines only, to achieve the narrowest exemption, accepting that context lines still block. — 2026-11-01 (widened by Q-4)\n\n",

Second occurrence after 2026-10-16.\n  Today: Q-2 keeps context lines checked.\n  Repository change: Options: A context lines of tests/ files exempt, removed lines checked; B keep Q-2 (added lines only); C the whole tests/ hunk exempt, removed lines included.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of committed test fixtures shown as diff context, facing repeated blocked reviews or a wider exemption, we decided to exempt context lines of tests/ files too while removed lines stay checked, to achieve reviews that pass over already committed fixtures, accepting that a committed test file's content reaches a reviewer that could read the file anyway. — 2026-11-22\n",

          "excerpt": "def check(\n    name: str,\n    denylist: Path,\n    root: Path = REPO_ROOT,\n    prompt_texts: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] = (),\n) -> Result:\n    \"\"\"Scan the scanned set under `root` against the denylist.\"\"\"\n    if not name or \"/\" in name or name in {\".\", \"..\"}:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no valid change name\",\n            \"Name the change folder under plans/changes/ (a single folder name). Without it the check cannot say what goes out.\",\n        )\n\n    rules, reason = read_denylist(denylist)\n    if reason is not None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no rule set to check against - the call does not start\",\n            f\"{reason}. Unchecked is not clean: without rules this script would report success over an empty set.\",\n        )\n\n    folder = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / name\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ does not exist\",\n            \"Without the change's artifacts it cannot be checked what goes into the call.\",\n        )\n    change_files = [p for p in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")) if p.is_file()]\n    if not change_files:\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ holds no file\",\n            \"An empty folder is a finding, not a scan that passed.\",\n        )\n\n    listed, why = _git(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--cached\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\")\n    if listed is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the tree cannot be listed\",\n            f\"{why}. What cannot be listed is not checked, and it would go into the call all the same.\",\n        )\n    result = Result(Verdict(), rules=len(rules), secret_rules=sum(rule.secret for rule in rules))\n    tree_files: list[Path] = []\n    link_texts: dict[str, str] = {}\n    unreadable = False\n    for part in listed.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\").split(\"\\0\"):\n        if not part:\n            continue\n        path, name = root / part, part.rstrip(\"/\")\n        if path.is_file():\n            tree_files.append(path)\n        elif path.is_symlink() and not path.exists():\n            # Nothing stands behind the link, but the link's own text is what git shows of it.\n            link_texts[name] = str(path.readlink())\n        elif path.exists():\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{name} is listed by git but is not a regular file\",\n                \"A link to a directory, a submodule, a repository nested in the tree or a special file: a \"\n                \"reviewer reads through it and this check did not. What cannot be scanned is not checked.\",\n            )\n        # else: listed and gone from the disk - nothing to read there; a staged deletion shows in the index scan.\n\n    scanned: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for path in (*change_files, *tree_files):\n        scanned.setdefault(path.relative_to(root).as_posix(), path)\n\n    hits = 0\n    for relative, path in scanned.items():\n        try:\n            text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        except OSError:\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{relative} cannot be read\",\n                \"What cannot be read is not checked, and it goes into the call all the same.\",\n            )\n            continue\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict, exempt=_under_tests(relative, path))\n    for relative, text in link_texts.items():\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict)\n    if unreadable:\n        return result\n    result.files = len(scanned) + len(link_texts)\n\n    staged, why = _git(\n        root, \"diff\", \"--cached\", \"--text\", \"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\", \"--no-renames\"\n    )\n    if staged is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the index cannot be read\",\n            f\"{why}. The index is what `git show :<path>` reads; skipping it would leave a staged value unchecked.\",\n        )\n    hits += _scan(\n        staged.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"),\n        \"staged changes (git diff --cached)\",\n      ",

          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

          "excerpt": "def _checked_probe(\n    runner,\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    endpoint: str,\n    model: str,\n    audit: list[str],\n    admission=None,\n    verb: str = \"prepare-explore\",\n    text: str = PROBE_TEXT,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The declaration, the exact-prompt leak check and the audit line - for this one probe, immediately before it.\n\n    `admission` (root, model -> problem or None) replaces the research declaration check for the review\n    swarm's free class (ADR 0021, decision 3); the leak check stays mandatory either way.\n    \"\"\"\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), root, [(\"prompt\", text)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise runner.Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the probe does not start.\")\n    # Re-read admission after the scan, which can cross the terms' UTC cutoff.\n    # Do not record a call or dispatch a probe on yesterday's admission.\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    audit.append(\n        f\"{verb} · endpoint {endpoint} · model {model} · leak check clean over \"\n        f\"{result.files} files, {result.commits} commits, {result.rules} rules.\"\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def _checked_probe(\n    runner,\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    endpoint: str,\n    model: str,\n    audit: list[str],\n    admission=None,\n    verb: str = \"prepare-explore\",\n    text: str = PROBE_TEXT,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The declaration, the exact-prompt leak check and the audit line - for this one probe, immediately before it.\n\n    `admission` (root, model -> problem or None) replaces the research declaration check for the review\n    swarm's free class (ADR 0021, decision 3); the leak check stays mandatory either way.\n    \"\"\"\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), root, [(\"prompt\", text)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise runner.Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the probe does not start.\")\n    # Re-read admission after the scan, which can cross the terms' UTC cutoff.\n    # Do not record a call or dispatch a probe on yesterday's admission.\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    audit.append(\n        f\"{verb} · endpoint {endpoint} · model {model} · leak check clean over \"\n        f\"{result.files} files, {result.commits} commits, {result.rules} rules.\"\n    )\n",

          "end_line": 3866,
          "excerpt": "def review_audit_only(before: bytes, after: bytes) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admit runner call lines under any heading, comparing all remaining input bytes.\n\n    Remove each call's blank separator with it and permit append's current-date\n    header stamp. All other bytes, including reviewer sessions and verdicts,\n    remain review inputs and must match HEAD.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    call = re.compile(\n        rb\"\\n\\nStage-2 call, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}: [a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?: \\(loop marks\\))?\"\n        rb\"(?: \\xc2\\xb7 attempt [1-9]\\d* \\xc2\\xb7 route [a-z0-9-]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 endpoint [a-z0-9-]+ \\xc2\\xb7 model [A-Za-z0-9_./:+-]+(?: \\xc2\\xb7 reason [^\\r\\n]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 leak check clean over \\d+ files, \\d+ commits, \\d+ rules\\.(?=\\n|$)\"\n    )\n    clean_before, clean_after = call.sub(b\"\", before), call.sub(b\"\", after)\n    if clean_before == clean_after:\n        return True\n    try:\n        stamped = check_frontmatter_current.stamped(clean_before.decode(\"utf-8\"), clock_now().local_date).encode(\n            \"utf-8\"\n        )\n    except UnicodeDecodeError:\n        return False\n    return stamped == clean_after\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2.py",
          "reference": "review_audit_only",
          "start_line": 3843,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false

        {
          "citation": "scripts/run_report.py::call_rows",
          "end_line": 318,
          "excerpt": "def call_rows(findings_text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The findings' Stage-2 call lines as bounded rows of explicitly recorded metadata.\n\n    These are evidence of a call, never measured attempts: no verdict is\n    inferred (a clean leak check is not a completion), absent fields say\n    `not read`, and rows are never joined on their attempt number.\n    \"\"\"\n    if stage2_runs is None:\n        return [\"  calls: not read (runner call reader unavailable)\"]\n    rows = []\n    for line in findings_text.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(stage2_runs.CALL_PREFIXES):\n            continue\n        matched = stage2_runs.CALL_LINE.match(line)\n        kind = matched.group(1) if matched else \"\"\n        rest = matched.group(\"rest\") if matched else \"\"\n        cells = rest.split(\" · \")\n        verb = \"session\" if kind == \"session\" else cells[0].strip() if len(cells) > 1 else \"\"\n        if not verb or len(verb) > FIELD_CAP:\n            verb = \"unparsed\"\n        fields = dict.fromkeys(CALL_FIELDS, NOT_READ)\n        verdict = \"verdict not recorded\"\n        for cell in cells if kind == \"session\" else cells[1:]:\n            key, _, value = cell.partition(\" \")\n            if key in CALL_FIELDS and 0 < len(value) <= FIELD_CAP:\n                fields[key] = value.strip()\n            if kind == \"session\":\n                dispatch = re.fullmatch(r\"dispatch (accepted|pending|failed)(?: \\(.*\\))?\\.\", cell)\n                if dispatch:\n                    verdict = f\"dispatch {dispatch.group(1)}\"\n        rows.append(\n            f\"  call: {verb} · attempt {fields['attempt']} · route {fields['route']}\"\n            f\" · endpoint {fields['endpoint']} · model {fields['model']} · {verdict}\"\n        )\n    return rows\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/run_report.py",
          "reference": "call_rows",
          "start_line": 284,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/run_report.py::CALL_FIELDS",
          "end_line": 76,
          "excerpt": "CALL_FIELDS = (\"attempt\", \"route\", \"endpoint\", \"model\")\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/run_report.py",
          "reference": "CALL_FIELDS",
          "start_line": 76,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "Three readers parse the audit line, and each tolerates a format change differently. `stage2_runs.CLEAN` is the literal substring `leak check clean over`, and the measure loop appends `(verb, CLEAN in line)`, so a line that renames or splits the phrase keeps its prefix but silently stops counting as clean. `stage2_runs.CALL_LINE` only anchors `Stage-2 (call|session), <date>: ` and captures the rest, so it tolerates any tail. `review_audit_only` in `scripts/stage2.py` is the strict one: its compiled byte pattern requires the exact tail `leak check clean over <n> files, <n> commits, <n> rules.` followed by a newline or the end of the input, and it only admits differences it can strip, so text appended after `rules.` makes a phase-6 audit-only delta fail. `run_report.call_rows` splits the line on ` · ` and keeps only cells whose key is in `CALL_FIELDS = ('attempt', 'route', 'endpoint', 'model')`, so a new count cell is dropped rather than reported."

          "excerpt": "def change_diff(root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The diff against the merge base with origin/main, uncommitted and untracked files included.\"\"\"\n    base = _merge_base(root)\n    flags = [\"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\"]\n    parts = [_git_output(root, \"diff\", *flags, base)]\n    untracked = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\").split(\"\\0\")\n    for path in filter(None, untracked):\n        parts.append(_git_output(root, \"diff\", *flags, \"--no-index\", \"--\", \"/dev/null\", path, allow={1: r\"\"}))\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n",
          "kind": "local",

        {
          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::free_diff",
          "end_line": 3077,
          "excerpt": "def free_diff(root: Path) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"The implementation diff the free swarm reviews, and what its own bounds cut from it.\n\n    The same merge base as `change_diff`, uncommitted and untracked files\n    included (criterion 3). Every file passes `_free_candidate`; each file's\n    hunks are bounded and the whole diff is, so no whole source file travels.\n    The second half names every cut, or is None: the round records it, because\n    a clean answer over a cut diff is no clean round (DL-A-1 of the deep review).\n    \"\"\"\n    base = _merge_base(root)\n    flags = [\"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\"]\n    changed = [name for name in _git_output(root, \"diff\", \"--name-only\", \"-z\", base).split(\"\\0\") if name]\n    untracked = [\n        name for name in _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\").split(\"\\0\") if name\n    ]\n    untracked_set = set(untracked)\n    names: list[str] = []\n    seen: set[str] = set()\n    for rel in [*changed, *untracked]:\n        if rel not in seen:\n            seen.add(rel)\n            if _free_candidate(root, rel, base):\n                names.append(rel)\n    parts: list[str] = []\n    cuts: list[str] = []\n    total = 0\n    for index, rel in enumerate(names):\n        if rel in untracked_set:\n            piece = _git_output(root, \"diff\", *flags, \"--no-index\", \"--\", \"/dev/null\", rel, allow={1: r\"\"})\n        else:\n            piece = _git_output(root, \"diff\", *flags, base, \"--\", rel)\n        bounded = _bound_hunks(rel, piece)\n        if not bounded.strip():\n            continue\n        if len(piece.splitlines()) > FREE_DIFF_MAX_LINES:\n            cuts.append(f\"the free diff of {rel} was cut at {FREE_DIFF_MAX_LINES} lines\")\n        parts.append(bounded)\n        total += bounded.count(\"\\n\")\n        if total >= FREE_DIFF_MAX_TOTAL and index < len(names) - 1:\n            parts.append(\n                f\"(the implementation diff was cut at {FREE_DIFF_MAX_TOTAL} lines; later files are not carried)\"\n            )\n            cuts.append(f\"the free diff was cut at {FREE_DIFF_MAX_TOTAL} lines; later files are not carried\")\n            break\n    return \"\\n\".join(parts), \"; \".join(cuts) or None\n",

          "excerpt": "def bounded_review_diff(diff: str) -> tuple[str, str | None]:\n    \"\"\"The prompt's diff, cut at `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES`, and what the cut left out.\n\n    The caller writes the second half into the round record: a clean answer over a cut diff is not a\n    clean answer about the change, and the record must say which of the two it was. The free round is\n    bounded too (R-12 of the review-swarm review): it carries the same diff, and an uncapped prompt\n    would read as a limit that is none.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Split on \"\\n\" only, as git counts: `splitlines()` also splits on CR and form feed, which inflates the\n    # count and rewrites the kept part's line ends (O191-4).\n    lines = diff.split(\"\\n\")\n    if lines and lines[-1] == \"\":\n        lines.pop()\n    if len(lines) <= REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES:\n        return diff, None\n    note = f\"the change diff was cut at {REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES} of {len(lines)} lines\"\n    return \"\\n\".join([*lines[:REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES], f\"## ({note}; the rest is not carried)\"]), note\n",

      "statement": "The diff text that a checked prompt carries is produced wholly inside `scripts/stage2.py`. `change_diff` returns the merge-base diff plus one `git diff --no-index -- /dev/null <path>` part per untracked file; `free_diff` builds the bounded per-file implementation diff, also with `--no-index` parts for untracked files, and records its own cuts; `bounded_review_diff` cuts either at `REVIEW_DIFF_MAX_LINES` and returns the cut note. `_review_round` assembles the paid prompt as the body of `prompts/04b-review-loop.md`, the round head, `ANSWER_FORMAT`, `READ_REQUEST`, `## The diff` and the diff, while the free round goes through `free_round_prompt(FREE_REVIEW_BODY, head, ANSWER_FORMAT, '## The implementation diff')`, which `free_probe_prompt` reuses over the bounded free diff. The same text therefore reaches `checked_prompt` (review) and `_checked_probe` (probe) by two different builders."

      "statement": "The by-hand and CI surfaces are deliberately narrow. `main` exposes `--name`, `--denylist`, repeatable `--prompt-file` and a suppressed `--root`, and `_read_prompt_files` labels each text with `path.name` only, so a hand-checked prompt arrives at `check` as `[('prompt', <file name text>)]` and never carries any hint of being a patch. `ci_gates.OHNE_AUFRUFER` lists `leakcheck.py` as a script with no step in the generated `ci.yml`, with the reason that it runs before every foreign call through `scripts/stage2.py` and needs a denylist kept outside the repository. In `scripts/kit/manifest.yaml` under `rules:`, both `scripts/leakcheck.py` and `tests/test_leakcheck.py` carry `rolle: mechanismus`, so the module and its test travel to instance repositories as kit content."

        {
          "citation": "scripts/leakcheck.py::_header_in_tests",
          "end_line": 202,
          "excerpt": "def _header_in_tests(line: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a diff header names a file under `tests/` - and only when that is certain.\n\n    With rename detection off, a `diff --git` header reads `a/<path> b/<path>`: the path is the one the\n    equal halves leave, which holds for a name with spaces too. A quoted name, or a header that does not\n    split in two equal halves, is not certain, and \"not certain\" is \"not under tests/\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if line.startswith((\"diff --cc \", \"diff --combined \")):\n        path = line.split(\" \", 2)[2]\n    else:\n        rest = line[len(\"diff --git \") :]\n        size = (len(rest) - 5) // 2\n        path = rest[2 : 2 + size]\n        if rest != f\"a/{path} b/{path}\":\n            return False\n    return path.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX)\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "_header_in_tests",
          "start_line": 187,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/leakcheck.py::_under_tests",
          "end_line": 207,
          "excerpt": "def _under_tests(relative: str, path: Path) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"A file of the working tree that the secret rules skip: under `tests/`, and not a link out of it.\"\"\"\n    return relative.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX) and not path.is_symlink()\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "_under_tests",
          "start_line": 205,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "scripts/leakcheck.py::_scan",
          "end_line": 241,
          "excerpt": "def _scan(\n    text: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    rules: list[Rule],\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    kind: str = \"file\",\n    *,\n    exempt: bool = False,\n    patch: bool = False,\n    first: int = 1,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Report each match as a place, a rule name and a length. Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "_scan",
          "start_line": 210,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],
      "statement": "The file-side exemption interface the prompt side must match is three constants plus two predicates: SECRET_PREFIX ('secret:'), TESTS_PREFIX ('tests/'), DIFF_HEADERS ('diff --git ', 'diff --cc ', 'diff --combined '), _header_in_tests (conservative on quoted names) and _under_tests (tests/ and not a symlink); _scan's exempt and patch switches are the only knobs by which a caller's text gets the per-file or per-hunk secret-rule lapse."

          "excerpt": "def begin_work_call(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    attempt: int,\n    route: str,\n    destination: Path,\n    reason: str | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Check and record one explore/implement attempt in its phase artefact.\"\"\"\n    result = checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    if destination == ctx.findings and not destination.exists():\n        destination.write_text(findings_header(ctx, producer_for(endpoint)), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    why = f\" · reason {reason}\" if reason else \"\"\n    append(\n        destination,\n        f\"Stage-2 call, {today()}: {verb} · attempt {attempt} · route {route} · \"\n        f\"endpoint {endpoint[0]} · model {endpoint[1]}{why} · leak check clean over \"\n        f\"{result.files} files, {result.commits} commits, {result.rules} rules.\",\n    )\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2_availability.py::_checked_probe",
          "end_line": 340,
          "excerpt": "def _checked_probe(\n    runner,\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    endpoint: str,\n    model: str,\n    audit: list[str],\n    admission=None,\n    verb: str = \"prepare-explore\",\n    text: str = PROBE_TEXT,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The declaration, the exact-prompt leak check and the audit line - for this one probe, immediately before it.\n\n    `admission` (root, model -> problem or None) replaces the research declaration check for the review\n    swarm's free class (ADR 0021, decision 3); the leak check stays mandatory either way.\n    \"\"\"\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), root, [(\"prompt\", text)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise runner.Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the probe does not start.\")\n    # Re-read admission after the scan, which can cross the terms' UTC cutoff.\n    # Do not record a call or dispatch a probe on yesterday's admission.\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    audit.append(\n        f\"{verb} · endpoint {endpoint} · model {model} · leak check clean over \"\n        f\"{result.files} files, {result.commits} commits, {result.rules} rules.\"\n    )\n",

          "citation": "scripts/run_report.py::call_rows",
          "end_line": 318,
          "excerpt": "def call_rows(findings_text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The findings' Stage-2 call lines as bounded rows of explicitly recorded metadata.\n\n    These are evidence of a call, never measured attempts: no verdict is\n    inferred (a clean leak check is not a completion), absent fields say\n    `not read`, and rows are never joined on their attempt number.\n    \"\"\"\n    if stage2_runs is None:\n        return [\"  calls: not read (runner call reader unavailable)\"]\n    rows = []\n    for line in findings_text.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(stage2_runs.CALL_PREFIXES):\n            continue\n        matched = stage2_runs.CALL_LINE.match(line)\n        kind = matched.group(1) if matched else \"\"\n        rest = matched.group(\"rest\") if matched else \"\"\n        cells = rest.split(\" · \")\n        verb = \"session\" if kind == \"session\" else cells[0].strip() if len(cells) > 1 else \"\"\n        if not verb or len(verb) > FIELD_CAP:\n            verb = \"unparsed\"\n        fields = dict.fromkeys(CALL_FIELDS, NOT_READ)\n        verdict = \"verdict not recorded\"\n        for cell in cells if kind == \"session\" else cells[1:]:\n            key, _, value = cell.partition(\" \")\n            if key in CALL_FIELDS and 0 < len(value) <= FIELD_CAP:\n                fields[key] = value.strip()\n            if kind == \"session\":\n                dispatch = re.fullmatch(r\"dispatch (accepted|pending|failed)(?: \\(.*\\))?\\.\", cell)\n                if dispatch:\n                    verdict = f\"dispatch {dispatch.group(1)}\"\n        rows.append(\n            f\"  call: {verb} · attempt {fields['attempt']} · route {fields['route']}\"\n            f\" · endpoint {fields['endpoint']} · model {fields['model']} · {verdict}\"\n        )\n    return rows\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/run_report.py",
          "reference": "call_rows",
          "start_line": 284,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {

          "excerpt": "def check(\n    name: str,\n    denylist: Path,\n    root: Path = REPO_ROOT,\n    prompt_texts: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] = (),\n) -> Result:\n    \"\"\"Scan the scanned set under `root` against the denylist.\"\"\"\n    if not name or \"/\" in name or name in {\".\", \"..\"}:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no valid change name\",\n            \"Name the change folder under plans/changes/ (a single folder name).           "excerpt": "def _header_in_tests(line: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a diff header names a file under `tests/` - and only when that is certain.\n\n    With rename detection off, a `diff --git` header reads `a/<path> b/<path>`: the path is the one the\n    equal halves leave, which holds for a name with spaces too. A quoted name, or a header that does not\n    split in two equal halves, is not certain, and \"not certain\" is \"not under tests/\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if line.startswith((\"diff --cc \", \"diff --combined \")):\n        path = line.split(\" \", 2)[2]\n    else:\n        rest = line[len(\"diff --git \") :]\n        size = (len(rest) - 5) // 2\n        path = rest[2 : 2 + size]\n        if rest != f\"a/{path} b/{path}\":\n            return False\n    return path.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX)\n",

          "end_line": 1936,
          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

one BLOCK aborts\n    # the round without a fallback (criterion 3).\n    checked = {\n        member: checked_prompt(ctx, endpoints[member], prompts[member], _free_admission(free, state))\n        for member in members\n    }\n    audited = 0\n    notes: list[str] = []\n    malformed_blocks: list[str] = []\n    try:\n        key = reviewer_key()\n        if not state[\"consumed\"]:\n            if state[\"free\"].get(\"skipped\"):\n                notes.append(f\"Notice: {state['free']['skipped']}.\")\n            if state[\"free\"].get(\"dropped\"):\n                notes.append(f\"Notice: free ids dropped: {dropped_notice(state['free']['dropped'])}.\")\n            for notice in state[\"free\"].get(\"notices\") or []:\n                # A same-host path move observed at discovery stays in the\n                # round's notes: the move is evidence, not a transient line.\n                notes.append(f\"Notice: {notice}.\")\n                print(f\"review-loop: {notes[-1]}\", file=sys.stderr)\n            skipped = skipped_models(root)\n            if skipped:\n                notes.append(f\"Notice: paid models skipped: {'; An invalid\n    pattern is named by its line number, never by its text.\n    \"\"\"\n    if not path.is_file():\n        return [], f\"the denylist {path} is missing\"\n    try:\n        lines = path.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").splitlines()\n    except (OSError, UnicodeDecodeError):\n        return [], f\"the denylist {path} cannot be read\"\n\n    rules: list[Rule] = []\n    for number, raw in enumerate(lines, 1):\n        line = raw.strip()\n        if not line or line.startswith(\"#\"):\n            continue\n        name, _, rest = line.partition(\"=\")\n        if rest:\n            name, pattern = name.strip(), rest.strip()\n        else:\n            name, pattern = f\"line-{number}\", line\n        try:\n            rules.append(Rule(name, re.compile(pattern), name.startswith(SECRET_PREFIX)))\n        except re.error:\n            return [], f\"the denylist {path}, line {number}, holds a pattern that is not valid\"\n\n    if not rules:\n        return [], f\"the denylist {path} holds no rule\"\n    return rules, None\n",

Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry.
