          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0014-a-change-claims-its-adr-files.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 147,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. The owner owes five interview answers of the maintainer,\n   whatever its class and its date.\n3. An ADR edit that no change of the work claims is a finding that names the\n   remedy. Nothing infers an owner from the paths a diff touches or from an\n   ADR's text.\n4. For a feature begun after its repository adopted the gate, the answer \"yes\"\n   comes with at least one claimed ADR file, and the answer \"no\" with none.\n5. The interview gate travels with the kit as mechanism. Each repository\n   records the day it adopted the gate; a change begun on or before that day\n   is exempt from the class minimums and from point 4, never from points 2 and\n   3. Moving that day is a decision pull request.\n\n**How it holds from this change on:**\n\n* The claim is the spec header field `adr_files`; the gate\n  `interview-minimums` (`scripts/check_interview_minimums.py`) holds points 2\n  to 4.\n* The day stands in `decisions/adoption.yaml`, a file that stays in its\n  repository; this repository's day is 2026-10-08, the day it adopted the\n  gate, so no change here moves between stock and subject. The gate reads the\n  day through `scripts/adoption.py`, which any other gate can call with its\n  own id (bead coding-harness-wpv); without the record the gate does not\n  measure (exit 3).\n* The gate script, its test, the reader and the reader's test travel as\n  mechanism (`scripts/kit/manifest.yaml`); the record stays as stock. An\n  instance such as LakeSwitch receives them with its next pinned Coding\n  Harness release (bead coding-harness-dj9).\n\n**What this record does not fix.** The field's name, the record's name and\nform, the reader and the gate's messages are the change's design: they change\nin an ordinary change as long as the five points hold.\n\nThis record amends no D- or O-number. It replaces the attribution of the\narchived change interview-minimums — the change folders a diff touches — and\nthe interim rule of pull request #126; ADR 0013 is unchanged.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture. A newly admitted\n   model takes a place in the review loop's ladder only; any other role\n   (explore, implem",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1559,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

      "statement": "The doctrine and decisions conflict on two points. First, docs/WORKFLOW.md and the leakcheck text state that a prompt text is not `tests/` (so a secret rule scans it whole), while Q-1 and Q-4 decide that `tests/` hunks of a prompt's diff are exempt; a test asserts the old behaviour (`test_a_prompt_text_is_never_exempt`). Second, Q-3 requires each use to be recorded 'in the findings.md call record', while the doctrine puts the audit line for Explore in `research.md`, the research swarm writes its call line plus a durable `leak_check` record through Run.audit, and a session writes its own 'Stage-2 session … dispatch pending.' form through stage2_session.audit_line — so 'every use' has no single stated record location."

Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. GLM 5.3 Flash explores a `bounded` change or a `spike` (a `feature` or `architectural` change goes to the research swarm, ADR 0020) and implements, and Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes (`repair <change>`, ADR 0017: a fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; phase 6 re-checks in a fresh read-only Codex session — a reviewer's own session never repairs); `explore <change>`, `draft <change>`, `implement <change>` and `repair <change>` are live;\n`--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 and records why when Stage 2 is off or Z.ai unavailable. A leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback. Reviews go by class, and so does phase 1 now (ADR 0020): a `feature` or `architectural` change explores through the research swarm (ADR 0020; a finder trio maps the sources, six seats research eleven topics, online topics on public sources only, Opus 5.5 reconciling; `prepare-explore <change>` first, its report shown to the maintainer, then `explore <change> --availability-reported <id>`; an aborted run resumes; the gate `research-handoff` holds interview and spec to the findings), a `bounded` change or a `spike` through GLM 5.3 Flash; `explore` reads the class from `--class` and the headers of `research.md` and `spec.md`, wherever stated, and refuses missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). Beyond that, explore, draft, implement and repair do not.\n\nPlus the session handover (the eighth movement — `docs/journal/handover/`,\n`direction: framework->framework`) and the question protocol:\n`[DECISION]` → human · `[GAP]` → explore, don't ask · `[DETAIL]` → agent\ndecides, reason into the artifact.\n\nBefore each fresh availability-enabled run, `prepare-loop` checks actual reachability with static, tool-free probes. Report its selected stages and failures in the main Claude Code or Codex conversatio",

          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Does the tests/ exemption reach the diff inside a prompt\n\nasked: 2026-11-01\nanswer: yes: diff hunks under tests/ in a prompt get the same exemption as the file - only the secret rules lapse, only for those hunks; the rest of the prompt and every other rule stay fully checked.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the secret rules over a diff sent as prompt text.\n  Intention: the review loop sends the change's diff as prompt text, so a fake key-shaped literal a new test assigns blocks the call (seen 2026-10-16 on coding-harness-omp, rule secret:generic-api-key-assignment).\n  Today: scripts/leakcheck.py skips the secret rules for files under tests/, but scans a prompt text whole.\n  Repository change: Options: exempt the tests/ hunks of the diff on the file's terms; keep scanning the whole prompt; drop the secret rules for prompts.\n  Architecture change: none (ADR 0007 boundary unchanged in kind).\n\nIn the context of diffs sent to foreign models, facing a blocked review for a fake test key or a widened exemption, we decided that tests/ hunks get the file's exemption for the secret rules only, to achieve reviews that are not blocked by test fixtures, accepting that a real secret committed under tests/ could reach a reviewer. — 2026-11-01\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included.           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0014-a-change-claims-its-adr-files.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 147,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen: option (1), with the inference removed, the reverse direction held,\nand the whole gate carried by the kit with a day per repository — because an\nattribution per edit needs the claim where the edit is made, one rule is\neasier to hold than an explicit rule beside a guess, and a workflow rule that\nholds in one repository alone is not a rule of the workflow (Q-1 to Q-5).\n\n**What is decided**, in five points:\n\n1. A change claims, in the header of its own spec, every file under\n   `docs/adr/` it creates, changes or removes. A later change that amends an\n   ADR claims that amendment itself.\n2. An ADR edit belongs to the change of the measured work that claims it. A\n   change that does not claim the file is no owner of it, whatever else the\n   work touches. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry.           "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock.           "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::The runner is the only way",
          "end_line": 1559,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it. Until that is built, `docs/WORKFLOW.md` §3 runs the two phases:\n   Haiku 4.5 explores and Sonnet 5.5 implements. This is an open item of the\n   change, not a claim that it works.\n6. **Endpoints are architecture; the models on them are declaration\n   (amended on 2026-10-30).** Which endpoints framework content may reach\n   stays this ADR's matter (decision 2) and its amendments'. Which models run\n   on a declared endpoint is set by `model-endpoints.yaml` alone, each through\n   a dated data-terms reading that the runner checks before every call.\n   Admitting, marking, removing or excluding a model there is a decision pull\n   request on that `human-decided` file, never an amendment of this ADR: the\n   OpenCode Go catalog changes too often to be architecture. A newly admitted\n   model takes a place in the review loop's ladder only; any other role\n   (explore, implem",

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021).           "excerpt": "def check(\n    name: str,\n    denylist: Path,\n    root: Path = REPO_ROOT,\n    prompt_texts: Iterable[tuple[str, str]] = (),\n) -> Result:\n    \"\"\"Scan the scanned set under `root` against the denylist.\"\"\"\n    if not name or \"/\" in name or name in {\".\", \"..\"}:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no valid change name\",\n            \"Name the change folder under plans/changes/ (a single folder name). Without it the check cannot say what goes out.\",\n        )\n\n    rules, reason = read_denylist(denylist)\n    if reason is not None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no rule set to check against - the call does not start\",\n            f\"{reason}. Unchecked is not clean: without rules this script would report success over an empty set.\",\n        )\n\n    folder = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / name\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ does not exist\",\n            \"Without the change's artifacts it cannot be checked what goes into the call.\",\n        )\n    change_files = [p for p in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")) if p.is_file()]\n    if not change_files:\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ holds no file\",\n            \"An empty folder is a finding, not a scan that passed.\",\n        )\n\n    listed, why = _git(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--cached\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\")\n    if listed is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the tree cannot be listed\",\n            f\"{why}. What cannot be listed is not checked, and it would go into the call all the same.\",\n        )\n    result = Result(Verdict(), rules=len(rules), secret_rules=sum(rule.secret for rule in rules))\n    tree_files: list[Path] = []\n    link_texts: dict[str, str] = {}\n    unreadable = False\n    for part in listed.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\").split(\"\\0\"):\n        if not part:\n            continue\n        path, name = root / part, part.rstrip(\"/\")\n        if path.is_file():\n            tree_files.append(path)\n        elif path.is_symlink() and not path.exists():\n            # Nothing stands behind the link, but the link's own text is what git shows of it.\n            link_texts[name] = str(path.readlink())\n        elif path.exists():\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{name} is listed by git but is not a regular file\",\n                \"A link to a directory, a submodule, a repository nested in the tree or a special file: a \"\n                \"reviewer reads through it and this check did not. What cannot be scanned is not checked.\",\n            )\n        # else: listed and gone from the disk - nothing to read there; a staged deletion shows in the index scan.\n\n    scanned: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for path in (*change_files, *tree_files):\n        scanned.setdefault(path.relative_to(root).as_posix(), path)\n\n    hits = 0\n    for relative, path in scanned.items():\n        try:\n            text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        except OSError:\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{relative} cannot be read\",\n                \"What cannot be read is not checked, and it goes into the call all the same.\",\n            )\n            continue\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict, exempt=_under_tests(relative, path))\n    for relative, text in link_texts.items():\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict)\n    if unreadable:\n        return result\n    result.files = len(scanned) + len(link_texts)\n\n    staged, why = _git(\n        root, \"diff\", \"--cached\", \"--text\", \"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\", \"--no-renames\"\n    )\n    if staged is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the index cannot be read\",\n            f\"{why}. The index is what `git show :<path>` reads; skipping it would leave a staged value unchecked.\",\n        )\n    hits += _scan(\n        staged.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"),\n        \"staged changes (git diff --cached)\",\n      ",

Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. Supersede before any new record exists in this worktree: a `review-loop` here can\n  start a fresh run when no audit call is unaccounted",

          "excerpt": "def review_audit_only(before: bytes, after: bytes) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admit runner call lines under any heading, comparing all remaining input bytes.\n\n    Remove each call's blank separator with it and permit append's current-date\n    header stamp. All other bytes, including reviewer sessions and verdicts,\n    remain review inputs and must match HEAD.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    call = re.compile(\n        rb\"\\n\\nStage-2 call, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}: [a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?: \\(loop marks\\))?\"\n        rb\"(?: \\xc2\\xb7 attempt [1-9]\\d* \\xc2\\xb7 route [a-z0-9-]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 endpoint [a-z0-9-]+ \\xc2\\xb7 model [A-Za-z0-9_./:+-]+(?: \\xc2\\xb7 reason [^\\r\\n]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 leak check clean over \\d+ files, \\d+ commits, \\d+ rules\\.(?=\\n|$)\"\n    )\n    clean_before, clean_after = call.sub(b\"\", before), call.sub(b\"\", after)\n    if clean_before == clean_after:\n        return True\n    try:\n        stamped = check_frontmatter_current.stamped(clean_before.decode(\"utf-8\"), clock_now().local_date).encode(\n            \"utf-8\"\n        )\n    except UnicodeDecodeError:\n        return False\n    return stamped == clean_after\n",

          "excerpt": "def _checked_probe(\n    runner,\n    root: Path,\n    change: str,\n    endpoint: str,\n    model: str,\n    audit: list[str],\n    admission=None,\n    verb: str = \"prepare-explore\",\n    text: str = PROBE_TEXT,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The declaration, the exact-prompt leak check and the audit line - for this one probe, immediately before it.\n\n    `admission` (root, model -> problem or None) replaces the research declaration check for the review\n    swarm's free class (ADR 0021, decision 3); the leak check stays mandatory either way.\n    \"\"\"\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admission is not None else research_probe_problem(runner, root, endpoint, model)\n    if problem:\n        raise runner.Refused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), root, [(\"prompt\", text)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise runner.Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the probe does not start.\")\n    # Re-read admission after the scan, which can cross the terms' UTC cutoff.\n    # Do not record a call or dispatch a probe on yesterday's admission.\n    problem = admission(root, model) if admi",

          "citation": "docs/adr/0007-stage-2-reviews-by-codex-and-glm.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 133,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. The runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) has no verb for\n   either phase yet, no plan marking assigns a step to Flash, and no effort is\n   set for it.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review.           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **Framework content may also go to `opencode-go`** — at\n   `https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/chat/completions`, through Pi\n   (`@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent`, at the version the runner pins), with\n   the three ids below. Of the stage-2 phases, the review loop (4b) only,\n   with the runner's `probe` that measures its rungs. The\n   sentence of ADR 0007 decision 2 that closes with \"Nothing else goes, and\n   nowhere else\" now closes with Codex, Z.ai's GLM and OpenCode Go; nothing\n   else goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to none of the\n   three. The interactive `session` verb reaches a declared endpoint under\n   its own amendment (bead coding-harness-amp); this declaration is what that\n   verb waits for before it opens its OpenCode path to the three ids.\n2. **The loop's reviewer role moves.** The loop leaves GLM for the ladder;\n   the spec review and the review stay with Codex exactly as ADR 0007 set\n   them (the maintainer, 2026-10-08), and phase 6 keeps resuming the\n   phase-2a session. Codex and GLM remain declared endpoints for what still\n   routes to them — explore and implement stay on GLM 5.3 Flash.\n3. **The ladder is data, not code.** Round *n* of the loop calls\n   `modelle[n-1]` of the `opencode-go` entry (the order at this decision;\n   the yaml is the truth and no doctrine text repeats it): round 1\n   `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, round 2 `mimo-v2.6-flash`, round 3\n   `mimo-v2.6-pro`. Rounds 1 and 2 both run, each still held by an undecided\n   row; round 3 starts only when round 2 wrote at least one row whose status\n   begins `taken`. The loop runs at most three rounds. Reordering the list is\n   a one-line pull request that touches `model-endpoints.yaml` and nothing\n   else.\n4. **The unconfined reads accepted for ADR 0007's reviewers extend to the\n   rungs — measured, not assumed.** A round has `read`, `grep`, `find` and\n   `ls` and nothing that writes or runs a command; but `read` reaches files\n   outside the worktree, and Pi has no switch that confines it. A rung can\n   therefore read what the maintainer's user can read — the secrets file and\n   the customer instance's checkout included — and send it to OpenCode Go.\n   What bounds it is the prompt's request to read nothing outside the\n   worktree and the repository's git directory: a request, not a lock. The\n   leak check scans what this repository presents, not what a rung reads.\n   The maintainer accepted this residual risk for reviewers on 2026-09-30;\n   it reaches the three rungs by this record.\n5. **The key stays in the runner.** It is read from the secrets file at call\n   time, reaches the call only in its environment as `OPENCODE_API_KEY`,\n   never appears in an argument or in a file the runner writes, and an\n   OpenCode Go call carries no other endpoint's key.\n6. **Each round is isolated, and Pi is pinned.** Each call gets a fresh,\n   empty Pi configuration directory whose one file switches Pi's own retries\n   off, a scratch home directory, and the switches that keep extensions, MCP\n   servers, skills, context files, prompt templates, themes, project trust,\n   sessions and every network request but the model call off. The isolation\n   was measured on Pi 1.1.0; the runner refuses any other version, and\n   raising the pin means measuring it again. The effort is Pi's `max`, which\n   Pi clamps to each model's ceiling — `max` for DeepSeek, `high` for both\n   MiMo rungs: a known limit, not a failure.\n7. **The address is measured before anything builds on it.** Three calls,\n   one per rung, run through the runner and Pi in phase 4 of the change that\n   carries this record — declaration and leak check in front of each, as one\n   special run whose commits are named in the pull request body. After the\n   probe, the change's own review loop runs on the ladder, at most three\n   rounds.           "excerpt": "def review_audit_only(before: bytes, after: bytes) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admit runner call lines under any heading, comparing all remaining input bytes.\n\n    Remove each call's blank separator with it and permit append's current-date\n    header stamp. All other bytes, including reviewer sessions and verdicts,\n    remain review inputs and must match HEAD.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    call = re.compile(\n        rb\"\\n\\nStage-2 call, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}: [a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?: \\(loop marks\\))?\"\n        rb\"(?: \\xc2\\xb7 attempt [1-9]\\d* \\xc2\\xb7 route [a-z0-9-]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 endpoint [a-z0-9-]+ \\xc2\\xb7 model [A-Za-z0-9_./:+-]+(?: \\xc2\\xb7 reason [^\\r\\n]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 leak check clean over \\d+ files, \\d+ commits, \\d+ rules\\.(?=\\n|$)\"\n    )\n    clean_before, clean_after = call.sub(b\"\", before), call.sub(b\"\", after)\n    if clean_before == clean_after:\n        return True\n    try:\n        stamped = check_frontmatter_current.stamped(clean_before.decode(\"utf-8\"), clock_now().local_date).encode(\n            \"utf-8\"\n        )\n    except UnicodeDecodeError:\n        return False\n    return stamped == clean_after\n",

          "end_line": 193,
          "excerpt": "# coding-harness — Agent Instructions\n\nThe home of the coding workflow: **seven phases, three stages**, the session handover, the kit that carries the process into new repositories, and the research corpus behind it. This repository is the source of truth for the process; `portfolio-agentic-engineering` and `lakeswitch-ai` run instances of it.\n\n**Status: bootstrapping.** The mechanism (WORKFLOW.md, prompts, templates,\nkit scripts) migrates from `portfolio-agentic-engineering` in measured steps.\nThe migration plan and current state live in the bootstrap handover:\n`docs/journal/handover/2026-09-16-coding-harness-bootstrap.md`.\n\nThis is the only instruction file: Claude Code (≥ 2.1.277) reads it itself, and\na `CLAUDE.md` would silently replace it (`tests/test_entry_points.py`).\n\n## The workflow in one screen\n\n| # | Phase | Artifact | Gate |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Explore | `plans/changes/<name>/research.md` | — |\n| 1a | Interview | `decisions.md` | the class minimums met — feature ≥ 3 · ADR change ≥ 5 (feature with ADR: 5 total) · spike 3 topics or reasoned skip · bounded 1 or reasoned skip — gate `interview-minimums` |\n| 2 | Spec | `spec.md` | validator green, no open `[DECISION]` |\n| 2a | Spec-Review *(optional)* | lines for `findings.md`, dimension SPEC | no open `[AMBIGUITY]` |\n| 2b | Design *(by class)* | `design.md` | validator green; an ADR draft when `architectural` |\n| 3 | Plan | `plan.md` | validator green |\n| 4 | Implement | code + tests | `make verify` green |\n| 4b | Review loop *(stage 2)* | loop rows, into `findings.md` after the phase-6 verdict | rounds until a clean round — the free swarm, the Flash swarm, then the paid ladder (ADR 0021); a targeted check after each runner repair and each orchestrator hand repair, the full `make verify` before phase 6 |\n| 5 | Verify | test output as evidence | stop-hook blocks on a red tree |\n| 6 | Review | `findings.md` | no open BLOCKER — `[DIVERGENT]` counts as BLOCKER |\n| 7 | Commit | pull request | CI green |\n\n**Stage 2** (framework content, ADR 0007 as amended by ADR 0011 and ADR 0016): a foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py`, which runs the leak check before every call. Codex drafts spec, design and plan (`draft <change>`; GLM 5.3 after two failed attempts) and reviews 6; Opus 5.5 reviews 2a (`spec-review <change>`); the review loop (4b) runs on OpenCode Go through Pi until a clean round (ADR 0021): round 1 is the free swarm, the models the `free_stage` rule selects from a forced live catalog refresh, on the implementation diff alone with no tools; round 2 is the Flash swarm, up to three cheapest reachable admitted paid models in parallel; then one id of the `opencode-go` entry's `modelle` set per round, cheapest first: the runner orders it by the declared `anfragen_5h` (requests per 5 hours, more is cheaper); a failed Flash member is replaced by the cheapest unconsumed one. GLM 5.3 Flash explores a `bounded` change or a `spike` (a `feature` or `architectural` change goes to the research swarm, ADR 0020) and implements, and Codex repairs the findings the orchestrator takes (`repair <change>`, ADR 0017: a fresh Codex attempt after a failed post-run check, then Sonnet 5.5; phase 6 re-checks in a fresh read-only Codex session — a reviewer's own session never repairs); `explore <change>`, `draft <change>`, `implement <change>` and `repair <change>` are live;\n`--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 or Sonnet 5.5 and records why when Stage 2 is off or Z.ai unavailable. A leak-check BLOCK stops without fallback. Reviews go by class, and so does phase 1 now (ADR 0020): a `feature` or `architectural` change explores through the research swarm (ADR 0020; a finder trio maps the sources, six seats research eleven topics, online topics on public sources only, Opus 5.5 reconciling; `prepare-explore <change>` first, its report shown to the maintainer, then `explore <change> --availability-reported <id>`; an aborted run resumes; the gate `research-handoff` holds",

          "excerpt": "def _scan(\n    text: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    rules: list[Rule],\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    kind: str = \"file\",\n    *,\n    exempt: bool = False,\n    patch: bool = False,\n    first: int = 1,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Report each match as a place, a rule name and a length. Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",

No\n   rendered copy is committed: the hosted CI hydrates, renders once and presets `BEAD_RENDER`; every reader goes\n   through `scripts/bead_render.py`. A fresh clone needs `tools/beads/install.sh && tools/bd bootstrap --yes` before\n   any tracker-reading gate can measure.\n3. **Use `tools/bd`, never bare `bd`.** The wrapper pins the version and refuses `init`, `migrate`, `upgrade` — the\n   three verbs that can change the shared database for everyone. The prefix (`coding-harness-`) was fixed at init and\n   cannot be corrected afterwards.\n4. **One writer per tracker, and one exception.** While more than one writing session runs in a repository, the\n   session that started first writes the tracker: it hands out beads, runs `tools/bd ready`, creates follow-up work as\n   `discovered-from`, closes, reprioritises and links. Every other writing session works in a worktree of its own and\n   writes exactly two things: the claim of the one bead it works on (`tools/bd update <id> --claim`) and its handover\n   comment on that bead — nothing more (ADR 0006, lakeswitch-ai D-60). At most `writing_sessions_per_repository`\n   writing sessions (default 2) run in one repository. Until the D-60 write guard exists, this is stated, not\n   enforced: the start hook and the status line show a second session, and a session that is not first checks before\n   any tracker write. After the writes run `tools/bd dolt push`. The push order is tracker first, git second: CI\n   renders the gate from `refs/dolt/data`, so a git push that outruns the tracker push merges against a stand the\n   commits claim to include — and goes red on exactly that gap (bead coding-harness-4t8).           "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When independent checks use the default setting, at most two protected admissions share the machine across repositories and worktrees, and both available slots can be reserved.\n   *Refuted by:* a third admission runs, or the eligible head waiter cannot reserve an otherwise free slot within two queue poll intervals (0.5 seconds at the default interval).\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-1`.\n\n2. When an independent entry requests capacity `1` or `2` through `HARNESS_VERIFY_SLOTS` (default `2`), effective capacity is the minimum of the settings of all live updated holders and the head live waiter; an older waiter counts as `1` and requires exclusive access.\n   *Refuted by:* a `1` holder shares capacity, a head `1` waiter enters before all holders drain, or two `2` entries cannot use both free slots.\n\n   Local child processes receive the setting when present; the foreign-model environment allow-list remains closed to `HARNESS_*` variables.\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-1`.\n\n3. If an independent entry has `HARNESS_VERIFY_SLOTS` set to anything other than the exact strings `1` or `2`, it refuses before protected work with a diagnostic naming the setting.\n   *Refuted by:* an empty, padded, `02`, `+2`, fractional or other invalid value starts work, or a valid inherited descendant is refused because of that setting.\n   *Basis:* `decisions.md#Q-1`.\n\n4. While independent live checks wait, the earliest registered live waiter, including an older checkout waiting exclusively, has first claim on capacity free under criterion 2.\n   *Refuted by:* a later waiter overtakes a live earlier waiter, a dead waiter blocks progress, or the eligible head waiter cannot reserve a free slot under the effective capacity within two queue poll intervals (0.5 seconds at the default interval).",

          "end_line": 38,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Does the tests/ exemption reach the diff inside a prompt\n\nasked: 2026-11-01\nanswer: yes: diff hunks under tests/ in a prompt get the same exemption as the file - only the secret rules lapse, only for those hunks; the rest of the prompt and every other rule stay fully checked.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the secret rules over a diff sent as prompt text.\n  Intention: the review loop sends the change's diff as prompt text, so a fake key-shaped literal a new test assigns blocks the call (seen 2026-10-16 on coding-harness-omp, rule secret:generic-api-key-assignment).\n  Today: scripts/leakcheck.py skips the secret rules for files under tests/, but scans a prompt text whole.\n  Repository change: Options: exempt the tests/ hunks of the diff on the file's terms; keep scanning the whole prompt; drop the secret rules for prompts.\n  Architecture change: none (ADR 0007 boundary unchanged in kind).\n\nIn the context of diffs sent to foreign models, facing a blocked review for a fake test key or a widened exemption, we decided that tests/ hunks get the file's exemption for the secret rules only, to achieve reviews that are not blocked by test fixtures, accepting that a real secret committed under tests/ could reach a reviewer. — 2026-11-01\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "## Q-4 · Context lines of tests/ files\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the exemption also covers unchanged context lines of files under tests/ (they are already committed and passed as test files); removed (-) lines stay fully checked; everything else of Q-1 to Q-3 stands.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: context lines in the diff of a tests/ file.\n  Intention: on 2026-11-21 an already committed fixture line (TEST_TOKEN in tests/test_verify_lock.py) entered the review-loop prompt as diff context and blocked prepare-loop; the orchestrator moved a helper to get past it (06c6414b, verify-two-slots). Second occurrence after 2026-10-16.\n  Today: Q-2 keeps context lines checked.\n  Repository change: Options: A context lines of tests/ files exempt, removed lines checked; B keep Q-2 (added lines only); C the whole tests/ hunk exempt, removed lines included.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of committed test fixtures shown as diff context, facing repeated blocked reviews or a wider exemption, we decided to exempt context lines of tests/ files too while removed lines stay checked, to achieve reviews that pass over already committed fixtures, accepting that a committed test file's content reaches a reviewer that could read the file anyway. — 2026-11-22\n",

Docstring and WORKFLOW state the exemption.\\n\\nCo-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>\\nClaude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_018qxAGMFNS3mM37eUEm5DuQ\\n\",\n  \"body_truncated\": false,\n  \"hash\": \"8c9ae9514bf7f96d931012ddfc091ee66d1c2ba3\",\n  \"subject\": \"feat(leakcheck): secret rules skip tests/, customer rules do not\",\n  \"touched_mapped_paths\": [\n    \"docs/WORKFLOW.md\",\n    \"scripts/leakcheck.py\",\n    \"tests/test_leakcheck.py\"\n  ]\n}",

          "end_line": 1559,
          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. Unchecked is not clean: without rules this script would report success over an empty set.\",\n        )\n\n    folder = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / name\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ does not exist\",\n            \"Without the change's artifacts it cannot be checked what goes into the call.\",\n        )\n    change_files = [p for p in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")) if p.is_file()]\n    if not change_files:\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ holds no file\",\n            \"An empty folder is a finding, not a scan that passed.\",\n        )\n\n    listed, why = _git(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--cached\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\")\n    if listed is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the tree cannot be listed\",\n            f\"{why}. What cannot be listed is not checked, and it would go into the call all the same.\",\n        )\n    result = Result(Verdict(), rules=len(rules), secret_rules=sum(rule.secret for rule in rules))\n    tree_files: list[Path] = []\n    link_texts: dict[str, str] = {}\n    unreadable = False\n    for part in listed.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\").split(\"\\0\"):\n        if not part:\n            continue\n        path, name = root / part, part.rstrip(\"/\")\n        if path.is_file():\n            tree_files.append(path)\n        elif path.is_symlink() and not path.exists():\n            # Nothing stands behind the link, but the link's own text is what git shows of it.\n            link_texts[name] = str(path.readlink())\n        elif path.exists():\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{name} is listed by git but is not a regular file\",\n                \"A link to a directory, a submodule, a repository nested in the tree or a special file: a \"\n                \"reviewer reads through it and this check did not. What cannot be scanned is not checked.\",\n            )\n        # else: listed and gone from the disk - nothing to read there; a staged deletion shows in the index scan.\n\n    scanned: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for path in (*change_files, *tree_files):\n        scanned.setdefault(path.relative_to(root).as_posix(), path)\n\n    hits = 0\n    for relative, path in scanned.items():\n        try:\n            text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        except OSError:\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{relative} cannot be read\",\n                \"What cannot be read is not checked, and it goes into the call all the same.\",\n            )\n            continue\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict, exempt=_under_tests(relative, path))\n    for relative, text in link_texts.items():\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict)\n    if unreadable:\n        return result\n    result.files = len(scanned) + len(link_texts)\n\n    staged, why = _git(\n        root, \"diff\", \"--cached\", \"--text\", \"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\", \"--no-renames\"\n    )\n    if staged is None:\n        return _refu",

          "end_line": 38,
          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Does the tests/ exemption reach the diff inside a prompt\n\nasked: 2026-11-01\nanswer: yes: diff hunks under tests/ in a prompt get the same exemption as the file - only the secret rules lapse, only for those hunks; the rest of the prompt and every other rule stay fully checked.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the secret rules over a diff sent as prompt text.\n  Intention: the review loop sends the change's diff as prompt text, so a fake key-shaped literal a new test assigns blocks the call (seen 2026-10-16 on coding-harness-omp, rule secret:generic-api-key-assignment).\n  Today: scripts/leakcheck.py skips the secret rules for files under tests/, but scans a prompt text whole.\n  Repository change: Options: exempt the tests/ hunks of the diff on the file's terms; keep scanning the whole prompt; drop the secret rules for prompts.\n  Architecture change: none (ADR 0007 boundary unchanged in kind).\n\nIn the context of diffs sent to foreign models, facing a blocked review for a fake test key or a widened exemption, we decided that tests/ hunks get the file's exemption for the secret rules only, to achieve reviews that are not blocked by test fixtures, accepting that a real secret committed under tests/ could reach a reviewer. — 2026-11-01\n\n",

          "end_line": 170,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nChosen option: \"Free swarm, paid Flash swarm, then single paid rungs until\nclean\", because it implements the maintainer's recorded answers, including\nthe corrected order and automatic free admission.\n\n1. **Clean ends the loop at every round number.** A completed round is clean\n   once every row is decided and none has Status beginning `taken` or\n   `fixed`; no rows or all rejected rows count. A clean free round ends the\n   loop before any paid review. This amends ADR 0011 decision 3's compulsory\n   second round, three-round cap and special round-3 admission rule.\n2. **Round 1 is the discovered free Go swarm.** Before each fresh loop run,\n   the runner forces `tools/pi/pi update --models` in its scratch agent\n   directory, then reads `tools/pi/pi --list-models` there.
