          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\n1. **D-13 is amended for framework content.** Criteria 3 and 4 stay, and the\n   runner (`scripts/stage2.py`) enforces them on every call: a green leak check\n   immediately before the call, and a declaration in `model-endpoints.yaml`\n   that clears the endpoint, the model and the data class — on a call of\n   explore or implement as on a call of a review. Criterion 2\n   governs lakeswitch-ai's content, which this repository never sends;\n   lakeswitch-ai's disclosure decision stays that repository's to write.\n   Criterion 1 is replaced by measuring the first three stage-2 runs, each\n   finding recording its reviewer, whether it was taken and whether it broke a\n   test, with a stop rule: after the third run, if at least one taken Codex or\n   GLM finding broke a test, stage 2 falls back to Opus 5.5 — Opus 5.5 reviews\n   every change, and phases 1 and 4 return to Haiku 4.5 and Sonnet 5.5 — until\n   the maintainer decides again (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). **The accepted loss is\n   the measured stage-1 baseline** before the first foreign call.\n2. **Where framework content may flow.** This repository's tree — the class\n   `framework` of `model-endpoints.yaml`: rules, templates, process, tests —\n   may go to `openai-codex` through the official Codex CLI, and to\n   `glm-coding-plan` through Claude Code: the reviews to Codex and GLM, and,\n   since 2026-10-06, exploration and implementation to GLM 5.3 Flash, which\n   read the repository broadly and write code into the worktree. Far more of\n   this repository goes to Z.ai than the review loop alone sends. Nothing else\n   goes, and nowhere else. Customer code and rows go to neither endpoint.\n   LakeSwitch and customer content never go, to any endpoint; the leak check\n   before each call is what blocks them. lakeswitch-ai's own trees are not\n   sent, and their disclosure decision (D-13, criterion 2) stays theirs.\n3. **Kimi is dropped, and so is Fable.** Kimi leaves the declared endpoints and\n   stands under `ausgeschlossen` with the date of 2026-09-30. Fable 5.1 leaves\n   the routing (2026-10-06); Opus 5.5 takes its places, the fallback of\n   decision 1 included. *The Kimi part is lifted on 2026-10-30 by decision 6.*\n4. **The reads of the foreign models are not confined.** They can read the\n   whole disk, the customer instance's checkout included. The prompts ask them\n   to read nothing outside the worktree and the repository's git directory — a\n   request, not a lock, and the doctrine says so in those words. The\n   maintainer accepted this as a residual risk on 2026-09-30, choosing it over\n   a proof of about one hour's work, for the reviewers. Explore and implement\n   widen what is read and add writes; whether that acceptance reaches them is\n   for the maintainer to confirm by merging this pull request.\n5. **Explore and implement run on GLM 5.3 Flash — decided, not built.** They\n   run there for every change, whatever its class: the class is stated in the\n   spec, after exploration. Unchecked is not clean: without rules this script would report success over an empty set.\",\n        )\n\n    folder = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / name\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ does not exist\",\n            \"Without the change's artifacts it cannot be checked what goes into the call.\",\n        )\n    change_files = [p for p in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")) if p.is_file()]\n    if not change_files:\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ holds no file\",\n            \"An empty folder is a finding, not a scan that passed.\",\n        )\n\n    listed, why = _git(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--cached\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\")\n    if listed is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the tree cannot be listed\",\n            f\"{why}. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names.           "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",

Without it the check cannot say what goes out.\",\n        )\n\n    rules, reason = read_denylist(denylist)\n    if reason is not None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no rule set to check against - the call does not start\",\n            f\"{reason}. What cannot be scanned is not checked.\",\n            )\n        # else: listed and gone from the disk - nothing to read there; a staged deletion shows in the index scan.\n\n    scanned: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for path in (*change_files, *tree_files):\n        scanned.setdefault",

          "end_line": 318,
          "excerpt": "def call_rows(findings_text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The findings' Stage-2 call lines as bounded rows of explicitly recorded metadata.\n\n    These are evidence of a call, never measured attempts: no verdict is\n    inferred (a clean leak check is not a completion), absent fields say\n    `not read`, and rows are never joined on their attempt number.\n    \"\"\"\n    if stage2_runs is None:\n        return [\"  calls: not read (runner call reader unavailable)\"]\n    rows = []\n    for line in findings_text.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(stage2_runs.CALL_PREFIXES):\n            continue\n        matched = stage2_runs.CALL_LINE.match(line)\n        kind = matched.group(1) if matched else \"\"\n        rest = matched.group(\"rest\") if matched else \"\"\n        cells = rest.split(\" · \")\n        verb = \"session\" if kind == \"session\" else cells[0].strip() if len(cells) > 1 else \"\"\n        if not verb or len(verb) > FIELD_CAP:\n            verb = \"unparsed\"\n        fields = dict.fromkeys(CALL_FIELDS, NOT_READ)\n        verdict = \"verdict not recorded\"\n        for cell in cells if kind == \"session\" else cells[1:]:\n            key, _, value = cell.partition(\" \")\n            if key in CALL_FIELDS and 0 < len(value) <= FIELD_CAP:\n                fields[key] = value.strip()\n            if kind == \"session\":\n                dispatch = re.fullmatch(r\"dispatch (accepted|pending|failed)(?: \\(.*\\))?\\.\", cell)\n                if dispatch:\n                    verdict = f\"dispatch {dispatch.group(1)}\"\n        rows.append(\n            f\"  call: {verb} · attempt {fields['attempt']} · route {fields['route']}\"\n            f\" · endpoint {fields['endpoint']} · model {fields['model']} · {verdict}\"\n        )\n    return rows\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2.py::checked_prompt",
          "end_line": 1936,
          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

          "citation": "Makefile::leakcheck",
          "end_line": 152,
          "excerpt": ".PHONY: verify test staleness gates leakcheck venv lock change index report close-merged archive help\n\nverify:\n\tbash scripts/verify_all.sh\n\ntest:\n\tpython3 -m pytest tests/ -q -n auto\n\nstaleness:\n\tpython3 scripts/plans_registry.py --check\n\ngates:\n\tpython3 scripts/ci_gates.py --list\n\n# Runs before a foreign call (scripts/stage2.py runs it itself) and never in CI:\n# it needs the denylist each machine keeps outside the repository.\nleakcheck:\n\tpython3 scripts/leakcheck.py --name \"$(NAME)\"\n\n# The interpreter must meet `requires-python` in pyproject.toml (the one place\n# the minimum is declared). Default: the first of python3.12, python3 on PATH;\n# `make venv PYTHON=/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12` names one. A wrong version\n# is refused before `.venv` exists, so no half-built environment is left\n# behind (bead coding-harness-y9q).\nPYTHON ?= $(shell command -v python3.12 || command -v python3)\n\nvenv:\n\t@need=$$(sed -n 's/^requires-python *= *\">=\\([0-9.]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' pyproject.toml); \\\n\thave=$$('$(PYTHON)' -c 'import sys; print(\"%d.%d\" % sys.version_info[:2])' 2>/dev/null); \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$need\" ]; then echo \"make venv: no requires-python in pyproject.toml\" >&2; exit 1; fi; \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$have\" ] || [ \"$$(printf '%s\\n%s\\n' \"$$need\" \"$$have\" | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n | head -n 1)\" != \"$$need\" ]; then \\\n\t\techo \"make venv: '$(PYTHON)' is Python $${have:-unknown}, but the lock needs $$need or newer.\" >&2; \\\n\t\techo \"Provide one, e.g.: make venv PYTHON=/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12\" >&2; \\\n\t\texit 1; \\\n\tfi\n\t'$(PYTHON)' -m venv .venv\n\t.venv/bin/python3 -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-ci.txt\n\nlock:\n\tuv pip compile pyproject.toml --group dev --universal --generate-hashes --exclude-newer \"$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z)\" -o requirements-ci.txt\n\n# The entry the workflow promises (docs/WORKFLOW.md, bead coding-harness-i0l).\n# NAME and BEAD are checked on the make level — given on the command line, never\n# taken from a stray exported variable — and the recipe passes them to\n# the entry script through its exported environment — their values are never\n# interpolated into the shell line, so arguments stay data, never code.\nchange:\n\t$(if $(and $(NAME),$(filter command line,$(origin NAME))),,$(error usage: make change NAME=<name> BEAD=<existing-bead-id> — both on the command line))\n\t$(if $(and $(BEAD),$(filter command line,$(origin BEAD))),,$(error usage: make change NAME=<name> BEAD=<existing-bead-id> — both on the command line))\n\t@export NAME BEAD; python",

Without it the check cannot say what goes out.\",\n        )\n\n    rules, reason = read_denylist(denylist)\n    if reason is not None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"no rule set to check against - the call does not start\",\n            f\"{reason}. Unchecked is not clean: without rules this script would report success over an empty set.\",\n        )\n\n    folder = root / \"plans\" / \"changes\" / name\n    if not folder.is_dir():\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ does not exist\",\n            \"Without the change's artifacts it cannot be checked what goes into the call.\",\n        )\n    change_files = [p for p in sorted(folder.rglob(\"*\")) if p.is_file()]\n    if not change_files:\n        return _refuse(\n            f\"plans/changes/{name}/ holds no file\",\n            \"An empty folder is a finding, not a scan that passed.\",\n        )\n\n    listed, why = _git(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--cached\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\")\n    if listed is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the tree cannot be listed\",\n            f\"{why}. What cannot be listed is not checked, and it would go into the call all the same.\",\n        )\n    result = Result(Verdict(), rules=len(rules), secret_rules=sum(rule.secret for rule in rules))\n    tree_files: list[Path] = []\n    link_texts: dict[str, str] = {}\n    unreadable = False\n    for part in listed.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\").split(\"\\0\"):\n        if not part:\n            continue\n        path, name = root / part, part.rstrip(\"/\")\n        if path.is_file():\n            tree_files.append(path)\n        elif path.is_symlink() and not path.exists():\n            # Nothing stands behind the link, but the link's own text is what git shows of it.\n            link_texts[name] = str(path.readlink())\n        elif path.exists():\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{name} is listed by git but is not a regular file\",\n                \"A link to a directory, a submodule, a repository nested in the tree or a special file: a \"\n                \"reviewer reads through it and this check did not. What cannot be scanned is not checked.\",\n            )\n        # else: listed and gone from the disk - nothing to read there; a staged deletion shows in the index scan.\n\n    scanned: dict[str, Path] = {}\n    for path in (*change_files, *tree_files):\n        scanned.setdefault(path.relative_to(root).as_posix(), path)\n\n    hits = 0\n    for relative, path in scanned.items():\n        try:\n            text = path.read_bytes().decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\")\n        except OSError:\n            unreadable = True\n            result.verdict.block(\n                f\"{relative} cannot be read\",\n                \"What cannot be read is not checked, and it goes into the call all the same.\",\n            )\n            continue\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict, exempt=_under_tests(relative, path))\n    for relative, text in link_texts.items():\n        hits += _scan(text, relative, rules, result.verdict)\n    if unreadable:\n        return result\n    result.files = len(scanned) + len(link_texts)\n\n    staged, why = _git(\n        root, \"diff\", \"--cached\", \"--text\", \"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\", \"--no-renames\"\n    )\n    if staged is None:\n        return _refuse(\n            \"the index cannot be read\",\n            f\"{why}. The index is what `git show :<path>` reads; skipping it would leave a staged value unchecked.\",\n        )\n    hits += _scan(\n        staged.decode(\"utf-8\", errors=\"replace\"),\n        \"staged changes (git diff --cached)\",\n      ",

          "end_line": 241,
          "excerpt": "def _scan(\n    text: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    rules: list[Rule],\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    kind: str = \"file\",\n    *,\n    exempt: bool = False,\n    patch: bool = False,\n    first: int = 1,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Report each match as a place, a rule name and a length. Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",

          "citation": "scripts/leakcheck.py::_header_in_tests",
          "end_line": 202,
          "excerpt": "def _header_in_tests(line: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a diff header names a file under `tests/` - and only when that is certain.\n\n    With rename detection off, a `diff --git` header reads `a/<path> b/<path>`: the path is the one the\n    equal halves leave, which holds for a name with spaces too. A quoted name, or a header that does not\n    split in two equal halves, is not certain, and \"not certain\" is \"not under tests/\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if line.startswith((\"diff --cc \", \"diff --combined \")):\n        path = line.split(\" \", 2)[2]\n    else:\n        rest = line[len(\"diff --git \") :]\n        size = (len(rest) - 5) // 2\n        path = rest[2 : 2 + size]\n        if rest != f\"a/{path} b/{path}\":\n            return False\n    return path.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX)\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_audit_only(before: bytes, after: bytes) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admit runner call lines under any heading, comparing all remaining input bytes.\n\n    Remove each call's blank separator with it and permit append's current-date\n    header stamp. All other bytes, including reviewer sessions and verdicts,\n    remain review inputs and must match HEAD.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    call = re.compile(\n        rb\"\\n\\nStage-2 call, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}: [a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?: \\(loop marks\\))?\"\n        rb\"(?: \\xc2\\xb7 attempt [1-9]\\d* \\xc2\\xb7 route [a-z0-9-]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 endpoint [a-z0-9-]+ \\xc2\\xb7 model [A-Za-z0-9_./:+-]+(?: \\xc2\\xb7 reason [^\\r\\n]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 leak check clean over \\d+ files, \\d+ commits, \\d+ rules\\.(?=\\n|$)\"\n    )\n    clean_before, clean_after = call.sub(b\"\", before), call.sub(b\"\", after)\n    if clean_before == clean_after:\n        return True\n    try:\n        stamped = check_frontmatter_current.stamped(clean_before.decode(\"utf-8\"), clock_now().local_date).encode(\n            \"utf-8\"\n        )\n    except UnicodeDecodeError:\n        return False\n    return stamped == clean_after\n",

          "excerpt": "def checked_prompt(\n    ctx: Context,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    admission_problem: Callable[[Path, str], str | None] | None = None,\n):\n    \"\"\"Check the admission and exact prompt immediately before one call.\n\n    `admission_problem`, when given, replaces the individual declaration (the\n    free class, ADR 0021 decision 3); the leak check is mandatory either way.\n    A subscription endpoint's expiry notice prints first (bead coding-harness-dcu3).\n    \"\"\"\n    subscription_terms_warnings(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise AdmissionRefused(problem)\n    result = leakcheck.check(ctx.change, leakcheck.default_denylist(), ctx.root, [(\"prompt\", prompt)])\n    print(result.verdict.render())\n    if result.verdict.exit_code() != 0:\n        raise Refused(\"the leak check is not clean; the call does not start.\")\n    # A scan can cross UTC midnight: an earlier admission cannot authorize\n    # dispatch after expiry, including retry and replacement calls.\n    problem = (\n        admission_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[1])\n        if admission_problem is not None\n        else declaration_problem(ctx.root, endpoint[0], endpoint[1])\n    )\n    if problem:\n        raise Refused(problem)\n    return result\n",

          "end_line": 5410,
          "excerpt": "def change_diff(root: Path) -> str:\n    \"\"\"The diff against the merge base with origin/main, uncommitted and untracked files included.\"\"\"\n    base = _merge_base(root)\n    flags = [\"--no-color\", \"--no-ext-diff\", \"--no-textconv\"]\n    parts = [_git_output(root, \"diff\", *flags, base)]\n    untracked = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"-z\", \"--others\", \"--exclude-standard\").split(\"\\0\")\n    for path in filter(None, untracked):\n        parts.append(_git_output(root, \"diff\", *flags, \"--no-index\", \"--\", \"/dev/null\", path, allow={1: r\"\"}))\n    return \"\".join(parts)\n",

          "end_line": 5586,
          "excerpt": "def run_git(\n    root: Path,\n    *args: str,\n    env: dict[str, str] | None = None,\n    stdin: str | bytes | None = None,\n    text: bool = False,\n    errors: str | None = None,\n    timeout: float | None = GIT_SECONDS,\n    allow: dict[int, str] | None = None,\n) -> GitRun:\n    \"\"\"The one launch of git in the runner (decisions.md#Q-8): the resolved `GIT`, run in `root`.\n\n    It forces the C locale over the inherited or supplied environment, so git's reason is English\n    and recognisable, and keeps every non-empty line of git's diagnostic in `diagnostic`. The\n    command fails closed unless both its nonzero exit code and its whole normalised diagnostic\n    match an explicit `allow` entry (a code mapped to a full-match regular expression). An empty\n    pattern handles only a silent status, such as diff's 1. One Refused error carries every\n    non-empty diagnostic line. A timeout raises\n    `subprocess.TimeoutExpired` for the caller to name; `timeout=None` waits as before.\n    \"\"\"\n    done = subprocess.run(\n        [GIT, \"-C\", str(root), *args],\n        input=stdin,\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=text,\n        errors=errors,\n        check=False,\n        env={**(os.environ if env is None else env), \"LC_ALL\": \"C\"},\n        timeout=timeout,\n    )\n    stderr = done.stderr if done.stderr is not None else (\"\" if text else b\"\")\n    diagnostic = git_error_text(stderr if isinstance(stderr, str) else os.fsdecode(stderr))\n    if done.returncode != 0 and (\n        allow is None or done.returncode not in allow or re.fullmatch(allow[done.returncode], diagnostic) is None\n    ):\n        raise Refused(f\"git {args[0]} failed (exit {done.returncode}): {diagnostic}\")\n    return GitRun(done.returncode, done.stdout, stderr, diagnostic)\n",

          "excerpt": "def _header_in_tests(line: str) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Whether a diff header names a file under `tests/` - and only when that is certain.\n\n    With rename detection off, a `diff --git` header reads `a/<path> b/<path>`: the path is the one the\n    equal halves leave, which holds for a name with spaces too. A quoted name, or a header that does not\n    split in two equal halves, is not certain, and \"not certain\" is \"not under tests/\".\n    \"\"\"\n    if line.startswith((\"diff --cc \", \"diff --combined \")):\n        path = line.split(\" \", 2)[2]\n    else:\n        rest = line[len(\"diff --git \") :]\n        size = (len(rest) - 5) // 2\n        path = rest[2 : 2 + size]\n        if rest != f\"a/{path} b/{path}\":\n            return False\n    return path.startswith(TESTS_PREFIX)\n",

          "citation": "scripts/leakcheck.py::_history_units",
          "end_line": 288,
          "excerpt": "def _history_units(text: str) -> Iterable[tuple[str, str, str]]:\n    \"\"\"Split the history text into (sha12, message, patch) per commit.\n\n    The split between message and patch is the marker line the log format writes, not anything in the\n    text: a message that spells out a diff header does not turn the lines after it into a patch.\n    \"\"\"\n    sha = \"\"\n    message: list[str] = []\n    patch: list[str] = []\n    target: list[str] | None = None\n    for line in text.split(\"\\n\"):\n        if line.startswith(COMMIT_MARK):\n            if target is not None:\n                yield sha, \"\\n\".join(message), \"\\n\".join(patch)\n            sha = line[len(COMMIT_MARK) :].strip()[:12]\n            message, patch = [], []\n            target = message\n        elif target is not None:\n            if target is message and line.startswith(PATCH_MARK):\n                target = patch\n            else:\n                target.append(line)\n    if target is not None:\n        yield sha, \"\\n\".join(message), \"\\n\".join(patch)\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "_history_units",

        },

      "statement": "Hunk classification rests on line-start matching of `DIFF_HEADERS` and on `_header_in_tests`, which returns False for any header it cannot read with certainty (a quoted or unequally split name), so 'when in doubt, the check blocks'. The history path is structurally protected against a forged header: `_history_units` splits message from patch on the NUL `PATCH_MARK`, and a test pins that a commit message containing a fake `diff --git a/tests/...` line still blocks. A prompt text has no such structural split — a prompt that embeds a forged diff header (the diff is concatenated into `_review_round.prompt_for`-style prompt bodies) would, under the new rule, move the scanner into the exempt state; today the pin is the opposite, `test_a_prompt_text_is_never_exempt`."
    },

          "end_line": 241,
          "excerpt": "def _scan(\n    text: str,\n    prefix: str,\n    rules: list[Rule],\n    verdict: Verdict,\n    kind: str = \"file\",\n    *,\n    exempt: bool = False,\n    patch: bool = False,\n    first: int = 1,\n) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Report each match as a place, a rule name and a length. Returns the count.\n\n    `exempt`: the whole text belongs to a file under `tests/`, so the secret rules skip it. `patch`: the\n    text is a patch, and each file's part of it is exempt on the same terms, by its diff header. A line\n    before the first header (a message) is never exempt.\n    \"\"\"\n    plain = [rule for rule in rules if not rule.secret]\n    in_tests = exempt\n    hits = 0\n    for number, line in enumerate(text.split(\"\\n\"), first):\n        if patch and line.startswith(DIFF_HEADERS):\n            in_tests = _header_in_tests(line)\n        for rule in plain if in_tests else rules:\n            found = rule.pattern.search(line)\n            if found:\n                hits += 1\n                verdict.block(\n                    f\"{prefix}:{number} - rule '{rule.name}' matches (length {len(found.group(0))})\",\n                    ADVICE[kind],\n                )\n    return hits\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/leakcheck.py",

          "excerpt": "def test_only_the_hunk_of_the_other_file_blocks_when_a_commit_touches_both(repo: Path, split: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"One commit, two files with the same text: the one under `tests/` is skipped, the other is found once.\"\"\"\n    write(repo, \"tests/test_a.py\", f'KEY = \"{SECRET}\"\\n')\n    write(repo, \"src/b.py\", f'KEY = \"{SECRET}\"\\n')\n    git(repo, \"add\", \"tests/test_a.py\", \"src/b.py\")\n    git(repo, \"commit\", \"--quiet\", \"-m\", \"both\")\n    sha = git(repo, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")[:12]\n    git(repo, \"rm\", \"--quiet\", \"tests/test_a.py\", \"src/b.py\")\n    git(repo, \"commit\", \"--quiet\", \"-m\", \"removes both\")\n    result = run_check(repo, split)\n    text = rendered(result)\n    assert result.verdict.exit_code() == BLOCKED\n    assert text.count(f\"commit {sha}:\") == 1, \"one hit for the hunk outside tests/\"\n    assert text.count(\"rule 'secret:planted'\") == 2, \"the same file's removal in the next commit is the second\"\n",

          "end_line": 598,
          "excerpt": "def test_the_exemption_follows_a_hunk_back_out_of_tests(repo: Path, split: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The file order of a patch is alphabetical: `src/` comes before `tests/`, and the state must not leak.\"\"\"\n    write(repo, \"src/early.py\", \"harmless\\n\")\n    write(repo, \"tests/test_late.py\", f'KEY = \"{SECRET}\"\\n')\n    write(repo, \"zzz/after.py\", f'KEY = \"{SECRET}\"\\n')\n    git(repo, \"add\", \"src/early.py\", \"tests/test_late.py\", \"zzz/after.py\")\n    git(repo, \"commit\", \"--quiet\", \"-m\", \"three files\")\n    sha = git(repo, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")[:12]\n    result = run_check(repo, split)\n    assert result.verdict.exit_code() == BLOCKED\n    assert f\"commit {sha}:\" in rendered(result)\n    assert \"zzz/after.py:1 - rule 'secret:planted'\" in rendered(result)\n    assert \"tests/test_late.py:1\" not in rendered(result)\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "tests/test_leakcheck.py",
          "reference": "test_the_exemption_follows_a_hunk_back_out_of_tests",
          "start_line": 586,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],

          "end_line": 82,
          "excerpt": "## Q-4 · Context lines of tests/ files\n\nasked: 2026-11-22\nanswer: A — the exemption also covers unchanged context lines of files under tests/ (they are already committed and passed as test files); removed (-) lines stay fully checked; everything else of Q-1 to Q-3 stands.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: context lines in the diff of a tests/ file.\n  Intention: on 2026-11-21 an already committed fixture line (TEST_TOKEN in tests/test_verify_lock.py) entered the review-loop prompt as diff context and blocked prepare-loop; the orchestrator moved a helper to get past it (06c6414b, verify-two-slots). Second occurrence after 2026-10-16.\n  Today: Q-2 keeps context lines checked.\n  Repository change: Options: A context lines of tests/ files exempt, removed lines checked; B keep Q-2 (added lines only); C the whole tests/ hunk exempt, removed lines included.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of committed test fixtures shown as diff context, facing repeated blocked reviews or a wider exemption, we decided to exempt context lines of tests/ files too while removed lines stay checked, to achieve reviews that pass over already committed fixtures, accepting that a committed test file's content reaches a reviewer that could read the file anyway. — 2026-11-22\n",

          "excerpt": "## Q-2 · Which diff lines are exempt\n\nasked: 2026-11-01\nanswer: only added (+) lines in tests/ are exempt; context and removed lines stay checked.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: which lines of a tests/ hunk the exemption covers.\n  Intention: keep the exemption as narrow as the bead needs.\n  Today: no exemption in prompts.\n  Repository change: Options: added lines only; added and context lines; the whole hunk.\n  Architecture change: none.\n\nIn the context of the exempt hunks, facing added lines only or wider, we decided on added lines only, to achieve the narrowest exemption, accepting that context lines still block. — 2026-11-01 (widened by Q-4)\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_the_report_never_carries_the_match(repo: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Thirty-two planted letters: no run of eight of them, and no pattern, in stdout or stderr.\"\"\"\n    write(repo, \"src/leak.txt\", f\"value = {SECRET}\\n\")\n    run = subprocess.run(\n        [sys.executable, str(REPO_ROOT / \"scripts\" / \"leakcheck.py\"), \"--name\", \"demo\", \"--root\", str(repo)],\n        capture_output=True,\n        text=True,\n        check=False,\n        env=os.environ.copy(),\n    )\n    output = run.stdout + run.stderr\n    assert run.returncode == BLOCKED\n    for start in range(len(SECRET) - 7):\n        assert SECRET[start : start + 8] not in output, \"a part of the match is in the report\"\n    assert \"[a-z]{32}\" not in output, \"the rule's pattern is in the report\"\n    assert \"src/leak.txt:1\" in output, \"without a place the finding cannot be fixed\"\n    assert \"'planted'\" in output, \"the rule's name is missing\"\n    assert \"length 32\" in output, \"the match's length is missing\"\n",

      "statement": "Q-4 (2026-11-22) widens the accepted consequence: unchanged context lines of tests/ files are exempt too, so a committed test file's content — the 'real key that is committed in a test file is not found' case pinned by `test_the_accepted_consequence_is_real_a_key_in_a_test_file_is_not_found` — now also reaches a foreign reviewer as diff context, with the maintainer accepting that the reviewer 'could read the file anyway'.           "excerpt": "def begin_work_call(\n    ctx: Context,\n    verb: str,\n    endpoint: tuple[str, str, str | None],\n    prompt: str,\n    attempt: int,\n    route: str,\n    destination: Path,\n    reason: str | None = None,\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Check and record one explore/implement attempt in its phase artefact.\"\"\"\n    result = checked_prompt(ctx, endpoint, prompt)\n    if destination == ctx.findings and not destination.exists():\n        destination.write_text(findings_header(ctx, producer_for(endpoint)), encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    why = f\" · reason {reason}\" if reason else \"\"\n    append(\n        destination,\n        f\"Stage-2 call, {today()}: {verb} · attempt {attempt} · route {route} · \"\n        f\"endpoint {endpoint[0]} · model {endpoint[1]}{why} · leak check clean over \"\n        f\"{result.files} files, {result.commits} commits, {result.rules} rules.\",\n    )\n",

          "excerpt": "def review_audit_only(before: bytes, after: bytes) -> bool:\n    \"\"\"Admit runner call lines under any heading, comparing all remaining input bytes.\n\n    Remove each call's blank separator with it and permit append's current-date\n    header stamp. All other bytes, including reviewer sessions and verdicts,\n    remain review inputs and must match HEAD.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    call = re.compile(\n        rb\"\\n\\nStage-2 call, \\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}: [a-z][a-z0-9-]*(?: \\(loop marks\\))?\"\n        rb\"(?: \\xc2\\xb7 attempt [1-9]\\d* \\xc2\\xb7 route [a-z0-9-]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 endpoint [a-z0-9-]+ \\xc2\\xb7 model [A-Za-z0-9_./:+-]+(?: \\xc2\\xb7 reason [^\\r\\n]+)?\"\n        rb\" \\xc2\\xb7 leak check clean over \\d+ files, \\d+ commits, \\d+ rules\\.(?=\\n|$)\"\n    )\n    clean_before, clean_after = call.sub(b\"\", before), call.sub(b\"\", after)\n    if clean_before == clean_after:\n        return True\n    try:\n        stamped = check_frontmatter_current.stamped(clean_before.decode(\"utf-8\"), clock_now().local_date).encode(\n            \"utf-8\"\n        )\n    except UnicodeDecodeError:\n        return False\n    return stamped == clean_after\n",

          "excerpt": "def call_rows(findings_text: str) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"The findings' Stage-2 call lines as bounded rows of explicitly recorded metadata.\n\n    These are evidence of a call, never measured attempts: no verdict is\n    inferred (a clean leak check is not a completion), absent fields say\n    `not read`, and rows are never joined on their attempt number.\n    \"\"\"\n    if stage2_runs is None:\n        return [\"  calls: not read (runner call reader unavailable)\"]\n    rows = []\n    for line in findings_text.splitlines():\n        if not line.startswith(stage2_runs.CALL_PREFIXES):\n            continue\n        matched = stage2_runs.CALL_LINE.match(line)\n        kind = matched.group(1) if matched else \"\"\n        rest = matched.group(\"rest\") if matched else \"\"\n        cells = rest.split(\" · \")\n        verb = \"session\" if kind == \"session\" else cells[0].strip() if len(cells) > 1 else \"\"\n        if not verb or len(verb) > FIELD_CAP:\n            verb = \"unparsed\"\n        fields = dict.fromkeys(CALL_FIELDS, NOT_READ)\n        verdict = \"verdict not recorded\"\n        for cell in cells if kind == \"session\" else cells[1:]:\n            key, _, value = cell.partition(\" \")\n            if key in CALL_FIELDS and 0 < len(value) <= FIELD_CAP:\n                fields[key] = value.strip()\n            if kind == \"session\":\n                dispatch = re.fullmatch(r\"dispatch (accepted|pending|failed)(?: \\(.*\\))?\\.\", cell)\n                if dispatch:\n                    verdict = f\"dispatch {dispatch.group(1)}\"\n        rows.append(\n            f\"  call: {verb} · attempt {fields['attempt']} · route {fields['route']}\"\n            f\" · endpoint {fields['endpoint']} · model {fields['m",

          "excerpt": "# A leak-check block stopped the research swarm\n\nOn 2026-11-18 the research swarm for `trust-pyramid-swarm` could not start.\nThe cause was not the swarm: the leak check refused, and it refuses before\nevery foreign call.\n\n## What happened\n\n1. `prepare-explore trust-pyramid-swarm --class feature` selected three Go\n   seats — `deepseek-v4.1-flash`, `glm-5.3-flash`, `mimo-v2.6-flash` — plus\n   `hy4-flash-free`. The intelligence index was not read\n   (`ARTIFICIAL_ANALYSIS_API_KEY` unset), so cost alone decided.\n2. The first run ended incomplete: `finders-0-2 (timed-out)` after twenty\n   minutes, and no later stage starts.\n3. `research-swarm-limits.yaml` raised `finders` from 20 to 40 minutes; this\n   repository has 1,117 files and about 4,670 commits.\n4. The second run stopped at the leak check with **BLOCK**.\n\n## The block\n\n- Commit `a890e90d`, \"docs(research): ontology as enforcement\", 18:15 on\n  2026-11-18, branch `ontology-relation-layer`, pushed to origin.\n- File: `plans/changes/ontology-relation-layer/research.md`, 32,122 lines.\n- Rule: `secret:connection-string-with-credentials`, match length 45, at two\n  places (commit lines 27861 and 27922).\n- **The matched text is not in this note.** The check never shows it, and\n  printing it here would spread exactly what the check exists to contain.\n\n## Why it blocks more than one run\n\nThe leak check runs immediately before every foreign call, and a BLOCK stops\nwithout a fallback (`docs/WORKFLOW.md` §4). Blocked are `explore`,\n`review-loop`, `review` and `repair`. Local work — gates, documents, pull\nrequests — is not affected.\n\n## What is not known\n\nWhether the match is a real credential or an example. The rule's exact shape\nlives in the machine's denylist outside the repository, so only the maintainer\ncan put rule and place together. Searches for URLs with userinfo and for\n`Key=Value` connection strings did not reproduce it; that says something about\nthe search patterns, not about the value.\n\n## The options\n\n1. **False positive.** The place is a placeholder; refine the denylist rule on\n   that machine. No repository change.\n2. **Real credential.** Rotate first, then decide about the history: the branch\n   is pushed, so a rewrite means a force-push and a garbage collection — and\n   the check itself notes that the reflog and the stash keep the value until\n   then.\n3. **Nothing.** Stage 2 stays blocked on every machine that runs this\n   denylist.\n\n## What was not done\n\nNo branch was rewritten, no value was shown, and the temporary copy made to\nlocate the place was deleted. The commit belongs to a parallel session.\n\n## State at the time of writing\n\n- PR #409, the research note on the trust pyramid, is **merged** (`f31d216e`).\n- PR #410, RB-A1 to level 4, is **queued** in the merge queue.\n- Bead `coding-harness-5kvq` and the change folder `trust-pyramid-swarm` carry\n  the swarm. The two finished finders sit in the research store and are reused\n  on resume.\n\n## The limits change in the same pull request\n\n`research-swarm-limits.yaml`: `finders` 20 → 40 minutes. It is the second\nraise of the same limit — bead `coding-harness-ht1b` raised it from 600\nseconds. Two raises for one repository size say the limit is not a constant: it\nshould follow the measured size, or the finder should report progress instead\nof timing out silently. That is a question for its own change.\n\n## Addendum — 2026-11-19, the outcome\n\n- **Option 1 was taken.** On 2026-11-18 the maintainer had the place\n  checked: a false positive, JSON-LD text in the research artefact of\n  `ontology-relation-layer` (commit 6df696e5) whose shape resembles a\n  connection string with credentials. No credential was exposed, and no\n  branch was rewritten.\n- The rule `secret:connection-string-with-credentials` in the machine's\n  denylist was refined so that a \"password\" starting with `[`, `{` or a\n  backslash no longer matches; the previous rule is kept as a dated backup\n  beside it. The next leak check ran clean.\n- The finder limit raise left ",

          "excerpt": "## Q-1 · Does the tests/ exemption reach the diff inside a prompt\n\nasked: 2026-11-01\nanswer: yes: diff hunks under tests/ in a prompt get the same exemption as the file - only the secret rules lapse, only for those hunks; the rest of the prompt and every other rule stay fully checked.\nanswered_by: maintainer\nstatus: answered\ncontext: |\n  Topic: the secret rules over a diff sent as prompt text.\n  Intention: the review loop sends the change's diff as prompt text, so a fake key-shaped literal a new test assigns blocks the call (seen 2026-10-16 on coding-harness-omp, rule secret:generic-api-key-assignment).\n  Today: scripts/leakcheck.py skips the secret rules for files under tests/, but scans a prompt text whole.\n  Repository change: Options: exempt the tests/ hunks of the diff on the file's terms; keep scanning the whole prompt; drop the secret rules for prompts.\n  Architecture change: none (ADR 0007 boundary unchanged in kind).\n\nIn the context of diffs sent to foreign models, facing a blocked review for a fake test key or a widened exemption, we decided that tests/ hunks get the file's exemption for the secret rules only, to achieve reviews that are not blocked by test fixtures, accepting that a real secret committed under tests/ could reach a reviewer. — 2026-11-01\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "plans/changes/leak-diff-tests-exemption/decisions.md",
          "reference": "Q-1 · Does the tests/ exemption reach the diff inside a prompt",
          "start_line": 24,

          "truncated": false
        }

      "statement": "The file-side exemption has a property a diff hunk cannot carry: `_under_tests` exempts a file only when it is under tests/ AND not a symlink ('a link under tests/ is not exempt — it can lead out of the folder'), pinned by `test_a_symbolic_link_under_tests_is_not_exempt`. Q-1 says prompt hunks 'get the same exemption as the file - on the file's terms', but a hunk in a prompt diff carries no symlink information; the two terms cannot match for a symlinked tests/ file. How the prompt-side rule resolves this is not stated in the decisions."

          "excerpt": "### The runner is the only way\n\nA foreign model is started only through `python3 scripts/stage2.py <verb>\n<change>`, never by typing `codex`, `pi`, or `claude` against another endpoint,\ninto a shell. Thirteen verbs exist:\n\n- `explore` — GLM 5.3 Flash for a `bounded` change or a `spike`, the research\n  swarm for a `feature` or `architectural` change (ADR 0020), phase 1; the\n  class is read wherever stated in `--class` and the headers of `research.md`\n  and `spec.md`; missing, invalid or disagreeing declarations refuse before any\n  model call; a swarm run needs `--availability-reported <id>` from\n  `prepare-explore`; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Haiku 5.5 and skips class derivation\n  and class/neighbour header checks; combining it with `--class` is refused\n  with exit 2 before any call. The runner states\n  the explorer's role and read-only tools in the prompt, and an answer that\n  names no file of the repository fails instead of being appended (bead\n  coding-harness-e7m).\n- `prepare-explore` — the swarm's preparation (Q-12): fresh Go catalog, tool-free\n  reachability probes, the six seats and their substitutes, a printed report\n  and a single-use receipt; refuses for `bounded`, `spike` and `--stage2-off`.\n- `draft` — Codex, phases 2, 2b and 3 in one call; GLM 5.3 (`glm-5.3`) after\n  two failed Codex attempts (\"The draft\" below).\n- `spec-review` — Opus 5.5, phase 2a, a headless call with read-only tools and\n  no session kept.\n- `implement` — GLM 5.3 Flash, phase 4; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses Sonnet\n  5.5 at effort `medium`.\n- `repair` — Codex, every taken finding of the loop record, the released\n  blocks and the phase-6 tables in one call; `--stage2-off [REASON]` uses\n  Sonnet 5.5 at effort `medium` (\"Repairing taken findings\" below).\n- `prepare-loop` — actual tool-free reachability probes for an availability-enabled\n  fresh run, a timestamped report and an external input-bound receipt; report\n  the selection in the main Claude Code or Codex conversation before using its\n  id with `review-loop --availability-reported <id>`. Each probe consumes a\n  request, times out after 60 seconds and retries a timed-out probe once with\n  a 180-second limit, preserving per-call leak/admission checks. A refusal\n  gets no retry. No repository content is supplied and no review round is counted.\n- `review-loop` — one round of phase 4b, started through Pi; round 1 the\n  free swarm the `free_stage` rule selects live, round 2 the three cheapest\n  reachable admitted models for an availability-enabled run (a legacy\n  declaration uses `flash_swarm`), then one eligible ladder rung each, until a\n  round is clean (ADR 0021). Exit 0 means a round was written, exit 2 a\n  refusal and exit 3 a loop that finished with a clean round (R-11 of the\n  review-swarm review).\n- `release-loop` — the loop rows into `findings.md`, after the phase-6 verdict.\n  With `--stage-failed <model> --reason <text>` it retires the stage that model\n  belongs to instead: the stage is consumed, the reason and a `## Stage failed`\n  block land in the loop record, every round row stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` continues with the next stage (R-1 of the review-swarm review).\n  With `--restart --reason <text>`, and only on the maintainer's request, it\n  restarts a completed loop (ADR 0021, restart amendment): one `Loop restarted:`\n  line lands in `findings.md`, every earlier round stays, and the next\n  `review-loop` is a fresh run — availability preparation, free swarm, Flash\n  swarm, ladder — whose round numbers continue (bead coding-harness-0xjr).\n  While another worktree of this repository holds an active record of the\n  change, the plain restart refuses and names those keys: the maintainer\n  supersedes them instead with `--restart --supersedes <key> --reason <text>`,\n  repeating `--supersedes` for every active other-worktree key the refusal\n  names. ## Runner exploration — 2026-11-23

## Research: leak-diff-tests-exemption (explorer output, English, ready to append)

Read-only pass with Glob, Grep and Read. Nothing was edited and nothing was run. `research.md` is 2.1 MB and was only sampled: its header, the start of its swarm section, and the `neighbours:` line. The swarm manifest body was not read.

### What exists today

- **Decisions already taken.** `plans/changes/leak-diff-tests-exemption/decisions.md` records four answers from the maintainer. Q-1 (2026-11-01): diff hunks under `tests/` in a prompt get the file's exemption, for secret rules only. Q-2 (2026-11-01): only added (`+`) lines in `tests/` are exempt; context and removed lines stay checked. Q-3 (2026-11-01): each use is recorded in the findings call record as a count of exempt lines, never their content. Q-4 (2026-11-22): context lines of files under `tests/` are also exempt; removed (`-`) lines stay checked. The file states that Q-4 widens Q-2. Status is `draft`, class `feature`, bead `coding-harness-juu`.
- **The check.** `scripts/leakcheck.py` (module doc and `check()`) scans five things: the change folder, the tree, the commit history, the staged diff, and any `--prompt-file` text. Rules whose name starts with `secret:` are skipped under `tests/`, by `_under_tests()` for files and by `_header_in_tests()` for diff hunks. The `patch=True` path in `_scan()` switches exemption per file on each `diff --git` header. Only a clean `tests/` path with the exact `a/<path> b/<path>` form counts; a quoted name is not exempt.
- **Prompt texts are never exempt today.** `_scan(text, f"prompt text {label}", rules, ...)` is called with `exempt=False` and `patch=False`, so a prompt is scanned whole with every rule. The module doc says so: "nor is a commit message or a prompt text."
- **Call sites that pass prompt text.** `scripts/stage2.py` `check_prompt`-style guard (around the `leakcheck.check(ctx.change, ..., [("prompt", prompt)])` call, near line 1923) runs before every foreign call. `scripts/stage2_availability.py` (near line 328) and `scripts/stage2_research_run.py` (near line 698, `self.runner.leakcheck.check(...)` with `slot.prompt`) do the same. All three pass the prompt as a single unlabelled `("prompt", text)` pair, so the check cannot tell a diff hunk inside a prompt from any other text.
- **Tests that pin today's behaviour.** `tests/test_leakcheck.py`:
  - `test_a_prompt_text_is_never_exempt` asserts that a secret-shaped line under `tests/prompt.md`, passed as a prompt text, blocks. Q-1 changes this rule.
  - `test_the_exemption_and_its_consequence_are_stated` checks that the module doc names the `secret:` marker and `tests/`. Any new wording must keep that check green.
  - `test_a_commit_patch_that_touches_tests_follows_the_same_split`, `test_the_staged_diff_follows_the_same_split` and `test_the_exemption_follows_a_hunk_back_out_of_tests` pin the whole-hunk exemption for commit and staged patches.
  - `test_the_report_of_a_clean_run_names_the_exemption` pins the report wording.
- **Denylist** is outside the repository (`LEAKCHECK_DENYLIST` or `~/.config/cc-routing/denylist.txt`). Nothing in the repository names its rules.
- **Where the call record is written.** `scripts/stage2.py` has `record_credential_scan_skips`, which "appends them at the end of the call record" (near line 9201), and a comment about recording scan limits "only in a contained regular call record" (near line 6308). This is the existing mechanism for appending a line to a call record. The Q-3 line (exempt-line count) has not been traced into it yet.
- **Recent history.** The git log names `d58b0ee1`, "runner records of a research run refused by the leak check (prompt line 39)". The subject line only; the refused run's content was not read.

### Where it lives

- `scripts/leakcheck.py`: `_header_in_tests`, `_under_tests`, `_scan`, `check`, `read_denylist`, `ADVICE`, module doc.
- `scripts/stage2.py`, `scripts/stage2_availability.py`, `scripts/stage2_research_run.py`: the three prompt callers listed above.
- `tests/test_leakcheck.py`: the pinned behaviour listed above.
- `plans/changes/leak-diff-tests-exemption/decisions.md`: the four answers.
- `plans/changes/leak-diff-tests-exemption/research.md`: a runner artefact (`research-swarm/v2`, run `7e5d5745…`, class `feature`, `neighbours: []`).
- No other `plans/specs/` or `plans/changes/` artefact about this topic was found by the keyword search; the hits in other changes concern the wider stage-2 or leak work and were not opened.

### What is unclear

1. **Whether Q-1 to Q-4 apply to prompts only, or also to commit and staged patches.** Q-1 and Q-2 name "diff hunks in a prompt". Today the commit and staged paths exempt the whole `tests/` hunk, removed lines included. Q-4 says removed lines stay checked, which, read literally, also changes those paths. The decisions do not say which reading is meant. Not resolved here.
2. **How the prompt diff is recognised.** `leakcheck.check` receives one `("prompt", text)` pair with no structure. Nothing shows how a diff hunk inside a prompt would be identified, or how a header would survive prompt assembly. The swarm and review prompt builders were not read.
3. **Whether the exemption count can be written to the call record.** `record_credential_scan_skips` is the nearest pattern. Whether it is the right place, and what line format the findings call record uses, was not traced.
4. **Unverified claim in the decisions.** Q-4 cites a 2026-11-21 block on `tests/test_verify_lock.py` (commit `06c6414b`). That commit was not checked.
5. **Unknown interaction with `test_a_prompt_text_is_never_exempt`.** It will fail once Q-1 lands unless it is rewritten to the new rule. Whether the maintainer wants it rewritten or kept as a guard for non-diff prompt text is not stated in the decisions.

### Which files a change would have to touch

- `scripts/leakcheck.py`: the prompt scan path (`check`, the `prompt_texts` loop) and the module doc paragraph on prompt texts.
- `scripts/stage2.py`, `scripts/stage2_availability.py`, `scripts/stage2_research_run.py`: only if prompts need labelling or structure to carry the hunk boundaries. Not decided.
- `scripts/stage2.py` call-record writer near `record_credential_scan_skips`: for the Q-3 count line.
- `tests/test_leakcheck.py`: `test_a_prompt_text_is_never_exempt` and new cases for added, context and removed lines; the doc test if the wording changes.
- `scripts/kit/manifest.yaml` (lines 142 and 231 point at `leakcheck.py` and its test) and `scripts/ci_gates.py` (line 127 describes `leakcheck.py`): checked for consistency only if the doc or file set changes.

**Open questions for the maintainer** (for the interview, not answered here): question 1 above, whether the commit and staged paths follow the new rule; and question 5, what becomes of the prompt test.
